translations.text: The word of God that came to Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judea, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judea, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem was taken captive in the fifth month.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you, and before you came out of the womb, I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
And I said, “You who are, Lord, Lord! Look, I do not even know how to speak, for I am a child.”
And the Lord said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am a child,’ for you shall go to everyone to whom I send you, and you shall speak everything I command you.”
“Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you,” says the Lord.
And the Lord stretched out his hand toward me and touched my mouth, and said to me, “Look, I have put my words in your mouth.”
“Look, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot and dig up, to destroy and demolish, to build and plant.”
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” And I said, “I see a walnut branch.”
And the Lord said to me, “You have seen correctly, for I am watching over my words to carry them out.”
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying, “What do you see?” And I said, “I see a boiling pot, and its face is turned from the north.”
And the Lord said to me, “From the north, disasters will flare up against the inhabitants of the land.”

“For look, I will call together all the kingdoms of the kingdoms from the northern land,” says the Lord. “They will come, and each will set his throne at the thresholds of Jerusalem’s gates, against all its walls all around, and against all the cities of Judea.”
“And I will pronounce judgment against them for all their wickedness, because they abandoned me, sacrificed to foreign gods, and bowed down to the works of their own hands.”
“But you, brace yourself, rise, and tell them everything I command you. Do not be afraid of them, and do not be dismayed before them, for I am with you to deliver you,” says the Lord.
“But look, today I have made you like a fortified city, like an iron pillar, and like a strong bronze wall against all the kings of Judea, its rulers, its priests, and the people of the land.”
“They will fight against you, but they will not be able to do anything to you, for I am with you to deliver you,” says the Lord.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, “Go and proclaim in the hearing of the children of Jerusalem, and say:”
“Thus says the Lord: I remembered you, the devotion of your youth and the love of your marriage, when you followed the Holy One of Israel.”
“The holy one of Israel belongs to the Lord, the firstfruits of his harvest,” says the Lord. “All who devour him will regret it; disasters will come upon them,” says the Lord.
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: “What fault did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me, followed worthless things, and became worthless?”

“And they did not say, ‘Where is the Lord, who brought us out of the land of the Egyptians and led us through the wilderness, through a vast, untrodden, waterless, and barren land, through the shadows of death, through a land that no one crossed and where no human being lived?’”
“And he brought us to Carmel to eat its fruit and its good things. But you entered and defiled my land, and made my inheritance an abomination.”

“And the priests did not say, ‘Where is the Lord?’ Those in charge of my laws did not know me, the shepherds acted wickedly against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed things that bring no benefit.”
Therefore I will still bring a case against you, says the Lord, and I will bring a case against your children's children.
Now cross over to the islands of Kittim and look. Send to Kedar and investigate very carefully, and see whether anything like this has ever happened:
Have nations exchanged their gods, even though they are not gods? Yet my people have exchanged their glory for things that will not benefit them.
The heavens were bewildered at this and trembled greatly, says the Lord.
For my people have committed two evils: they abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and dug themselves cisterns—leaking cisterns that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a servant, or Jacob a slave? Why have they become plunder?
Lions roared against him and raised their voices. They made his land a wasteland, and his cities were destroyed, with no inhabitants left.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes recognized you and mocked you.
Was it not your abandoning me that brought this upon you, says the Lord your God, when I was leading you along the way?
And now, what have you to do with the road to Egypt, that you should drink the water of the Gihon? And what have you to do with the road to Assyria, that you should drink the water of its rivers?

Your rebellion will discipline you, and your evil deeds will rebuke you. You will know and see that it is evil and bitter for you to abandon me, says the Lord your God. And I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

For long ago you broke your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and you said, ‘I will not serve. Instead, I will go upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree, and there I will abandon myself to prostitution.’
But I planted you as a fruitful vine, entirely genuine. How have you turned bitter toward me, a vine gone foreign?
Even if you wash yourself with lye and use plenty of soap, you remain stained by your wrongdoing before me, says the Lord God.
How can you say, ‘I have not defiled myself, and I have not followed Baal’? Look at your paths among the tombs, and know what you have done.

In the evening the sound of her weeping cried out along her paths. She abounded in the waters of the wilderness; in the desire of her soul she was seized by a demon. She was handed over, and who will turn her back? All who seek her will not grow weary; in her distress you will find her.
Turn your heart away from the harsh road and your throat from thirst. But she says, ‘I can,’ for she loved strangers and followed them.
As a thief is ashamed when caught, so the children of Israel will be ashamed—they themselves, their kings, their rulers, their priests, and their prophets.
They said to wood, ‘You are my father,’ and to stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’ They turned their backs to me, not their faces. Yet in the time of their troubles they will say, ‘Arise and save us!’

And where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them arise and save you in the time of your troubles. For your gods were as many as your cities, Judah, and they sacrificed to Baal in as many places as there were streets in Jerusalem.
Now why do you argue with me? For all of you have acted wickedly, and all of you have acted lawlessly against me, says the Lord.
In vain I struck your children, and you accepted no correction. The sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion, and you were not terrified.

Hear the words of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Have I been a wilderness to the house of Israel, or a ruined, uncultivated land? Why did my people say, ‘We will wander without a master, and we will not come to you’?
Can a maiden forget her ornaments, or a bride her beautifully adorned sash? Yet my people have forgotten me for countless days.
What further good will you devise in your ways to seek reconciliation? And not only that: you yourself have also acted wickedly, defiling your ways.
And on your hands was found the blood of innocent poor people. I did not find them in pits, but under every oak.
And you said, “I am innocent; let his anger turn away from me.” Look, I will bring you to judgment because you said, “I have not sinned.”
Why did you so greatly disdain retracing your paths? You will be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria.
For you will leave there too with your hands on your head, because the Lord has rejected what you trusted in, and you will no longer prosper through it.

If a man dismisses his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man’s wife, will she return again to the same man? Would that woman not be utterly defiled? You have prostituted yourself with many lovers, yet return to me, says the Lord.

Lift your eyes straight ahead and see: where have you not been defiled? On your roads you sat waiting for them, like a solitary raven in a deserted place. You defiled your land with your prostitution and your evil deeds.
And you acquired many shepherds to bring about your downfall. Your face became that of a prostitute; you were shameless before everyone.
Did you not call me your home, your father, and the ruler of your virginity?
Will he remain angry forever, or preserve his anger to the end? Look, you have spoken and done all these evil things, and you have grown strong.

And the Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah, “Have you seen what the community of Israel has done? She went off by herself onto every high mountain and under every thickly wooded tree, and prostituted herself there.”
And after all her prostitution I said, “Return to me.” But she did not return, and faithless Judah saw her debauchery.

And I saw that the community of Israel was caught in all her acts of adultery. I dismissed her and put a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet her sister, faithless Judah, was not afraid, but went and prostituted herself too.
And her prostitution was treated as nothing, and she polluted the land, for she committed adultery with stone and wood.
And despite all this, her faithless sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but deceitfully, says the Lord.
And the Lord said to me, “Israel’s rebellion has shown itself righteous compared with Judah’s faithlessness.”

Now go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, “Return to me, community of Israel, says the Lord. I will not set my face against you, for I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not hold a grudge against you forever.”
Only acknowledge your wrongdoing: you acted wickedly against the Lord your God, and spread your paths toward strangers under every thickly wooded tree, and did not listen to my voice, says the Lord.
Return to me, children who have gone away, says the Lord, for I have been your master. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will tend you with wisdom.

And when you multiply and increase in the land in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, “The ark of the covenants of the Holy One of Israel.” It will not come to mind, nor will it be mentioned, nor will it be sought or made again.
At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all nations will gather in Jerusalem in the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the schemes of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Israel will gather with the house of Judah, and they will come together from the north and from every region to the land that I gave their ancestors as an inheritance.

And I say, “May it be so, Lord, for I will place you among the children and give you the choice land, a renowned inheritance of Almighty God of the nations.” And I said, “You will call me Father, and you will no longer turn away from me.”
But as a woman scorns her husband, so the house of Israel has scorned me, says the Lord.
A voice cried out from the lips of the children of Israel in weeping and supplication, because they had acted unjustly in their ways and forgotten their holy God.
Return, you wandering children, and I will heal your brokenness. And they said, “Here we are, for you are the Lord our God.”
Indeed, the hills and the powers of the heights were false, but the salvation of Israel is through the Lord our God.
And shame consumed the labor of our fathers from their youth: their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.
We lay down in our shame, and our disgrace covered us, because we and our fathers have sinned before our God from our youth until this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God.
If Israel returns to me, says the Lord, he shall return; and if he casts his abominations out of his mouth for the sake of the God of Jerusalem, he will fear before me,
and swears, “As the Lord lives,” in truth, justice, and righteousness, the nations will be blessed through him and will boast in him.
For this is what the Lord says to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Plow your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves for your God, and cut away the uncircumcision of your hearts, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my wrath go out like fire and blaze with no one to quench it because of your evil deeds.
Announce the news in Judea, and let it be heard in Jerusalem. Say, “Sound the trumpet throughout the land! Raise a cry and proclaim, ‘Gather together, and let us enter the fortified cities!’”
Set out and flee to Zion! Hurry, do not stand still, for I will bring calamity from the north and great destruction.
A lion has come out of his thicket. He has set out to destroy nations and has left his place to make your land a wasteland. Your cities will be torn down, with no inhabitants in them.
Because of this, put on sackcloth, mourn, and raise a cry, for the Lord’s fierce anger has not turned away from us.
And on that day, says the Lord, the king and the rulers will lose heart; the priests will become foolish, and the prophets will be astonished.
And I say, “O Lord, Lord, you have indeed utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, for you said, ‘You will have peace,’ yet the sword will reach their very lives.”
At that time you will say to this people and to Jerusalem: A wind of deception in the wilderness, on the path of the daughter of my people, neither for cleansing nor for purification.
A wind at full strength will come to me from them. From now on I will speak to them with my judgments.
Behold, he will rise like a cloud, and his chariots are like a whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will thoughts of your afflictions be found within you?
For there is the voice of a messenger of bad news from Dan, and troubles will be heard of from Mount Ephraim.
Remind the nations: behold, they have arrived in Jerusalem. Announce that troops are coming from a distant land; they have raised their voices against the cities of Judea.
Like guards of a field, they surrounded her, because you neglected me, says the Lord.
Your way and your conduct have brought all this upon you. This is your wickedness and bitterness, for it has reached your heart.

My belly, my belly and the sensitive parts of my heart ache! My heart groans and writhes, and my soul will not be still, for you have heard, my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the news of war and misery.
Raise an outcry of destruction upon destruction, for the whole land has been devastated. Suddenly the tent has been devastated, and the flaps of my tent have been torn down.
How long must I see fugitives and hear the sound of the trumpet?
For the rulers of my people did not know me. They are senseless children and have no understanding. They are wise at doing evil, but they do not know how to do anything good.
I looked at the earth, and behold, it was empty and there was nothing there; and at the heavens, and they had no light.
I saw the mountains trembling, and all the hills in turmoil.
I looked, and there was no one, and all the birds of heaven trembled.
I saw, and Carmel was desolate, and all its cities were burned and destroyed before the Lord and before his fierce anger.
Thus says the Lord: The whole land will be laid waste, but I will not make a complete end of it.
Because of all this, the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark, for I have spoken and will not regret it; I have resolved and will not turn back from it.
At the sound of horsemen and fully drawn bows, the whole land fled. They crept into caves, hid in forests, and went into rocky caverns. Every city was abandoned, and no one lived in them.

And you, wretched one, what will you do? Even if you dress in scarlet, adorn yourself with gold ornaments, and apply antimony to your eyes, your adornments are in vain. Your lovers have rejected you and seek your life.

For I heard a voice like the labor pains of a woman bearing her first child, the sound of your groaning, daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: “Woe to me, for my life is failing because of those who kill!”

Go back and forth through the streets of Jerusalem. Look and find out, and search its squares to see whether you can find one man who practices justice and seeks faithfulness, and I will pardon them, says the Lord.
Even if they say, “As the Lord lives,” they still swear falsely.

Lord, your eyes look for faithfulness. You afflicted them, but they felt no pain. You brought them to an end, but they refused to accept correction. They made their faces harder than rock and refused to turn back.
And I said: Perhaps they are poor; therefore they could not understand the ways of the Lord and the judgments of God.
I will go to the rich and speak with them, for they know the way of the Lord and the judgment of God. But they too, all together, broke the yoke and tore apart the harness straps.

Therefore a lion from the forest struck them, and a wolf destroyed them even in their houses. A leopard kept watch over their cities, and everyone who goes out from them will fall dead, because they multiplied their ungodliness and grew strong in their rebellion.
For which of these things shall I be reconciled with you? Your children abandoned me and swore by those that are not gods. I fed them to the full, but they committed adultery and lodged in brothels.
They became stallions eager for mares; each neighed for his neighbor’s wife.
Shall I not call them to account for all this, says the Lord? Shall my soul not seek vengeance on such a nation?
Go up onto its battlements and destroy them, but do not make a complete end. Leave its foundations, for they belong to the Lord.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have utterly despised me, says the Lord.
They lied to their Lord and say, “That is nothing. No calamities will come upon us, and we will see neither sword nor famine.”
Our prophets became wind, and the word of the Lord was not in them. So may it happen to them.
Therefore this is what the Lord God Almighty says: Because you spoke these words, look, I have made my word in your mouth fire, and this people wood, and it will consume them.

For look, I will bring a nation from far away against you, house of Israel, says the Lord: an ancient nation, a nation from ages past, a nation whose language you will not understand and whose words you will not comprehend.
Their quivers are like open graves; they are all mighty warriors.

They will eat your harvest and your bread, and they will eat your sons and daughters. They will eat your sheep and cattle, and they will eat your vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees. They will demolish your strongly fortified cities, in which you boast; they will destroy them with the sword.
And on that day, says the Lord your God, I will not make a complete end of you.

And when you say, “Why has the Lord our God done all this to us?” you shall say to them, “Because you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, you will likewise serve foreigners in a land that is not yours.”
Declare this in the house of Jacob, and let it be heard in the house of Judah, and say:
Hear this, foolish and senseless people, who have eyes but do not see, and ears but do not hear.

Will you not fear me, says the Lord, or tremble before me? I established the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting decree that it shall not cross. It may rage, but it cannot come out; its waves may roar, but they shall not cross it.
But this people had a disobedient and defiant heart. They went astray, turned aside, and departed.
And they did not say in their hearts, “Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and late rains at the proper time for fulfilling the appointed harvest, and who will preserve us.”
Our lawless deeds have turned this aside, and our sins have kept good things away from us.
For wicked people were found among my people, and they set up snares like those of birdcatchers to destroy people.
And they caught them. Like sprung traps full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Because of this they became prosperous and great.

They grew fat and stout, and they transgressed my words in wickedness. They did not judge with righteous judgment; they did not uphold the rights of the orphan, and they did not judge the widow’s case.
Shall I not call them to account for all this, says the Lord? Shall my soul not seek vengeance on such a nation?
Foolish and terrifying things have happened in the land.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests applaud them, and my people loved this. And what will you do afterward?

Be strong, children of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem. Sound the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for evils come looming from the north, and there will be great destruction
for the beautiful and pampered one; and your loftiness will be taken away, daughter of Zion.
Shepherds and their flocks will come to her, and they will pitch their tents around her, and each will pasture his flock with his own hand.
Prepare for war against her. Rise, and let us go up against her at noon. Woe to us, for the day has grown short, and the evening shadows have reached us.
Rise, and let us go up by night and destroy her foundations.
For this is what the Lord of hosts says: Break down her wooden structures; cast an army against Jerusalem, for she is a city wholly false, with oppression within her.
As a cistern cools its water, so she cools her evils. Ungodliness and wickedness will be heard within her; pain and torment are continually before her.
Accept correction, Jerusalem, lest my soul depart from you, lest I make you a wilderness, a land where no one has ever lived.
For thus says the Lord of hosts: “Glean, glean; gather the remaining grapes of the remnant of Israel, and turn back again like a grape-gatherer to his basket.”

To whom shall I speak, and to whom shall I bear witness, so that they will listen? Look, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Look, the word of the Lord has become an object of reproach to them, and they will no longer delight in it.

And I filled up my anger and restrained it, and did not put an end to them. I will pour it out upon the children outside and upon the gathering of young men together, for husband and wife will be captured together; the old man and the one advanced in years will be driven back.
And their houses will be seized by strangers, their fields and their wives together, for I will stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of that land, says the Lord.
For from their least to their greatest, they have all committed lawless deeds; from the priest to the false prophet, they have all acted falsely.
And they treated the wounds of the daughter of my people with contempt, saying, “Peace, peace!” But where is peace?

Were they ashamed because they had fallen short? They did not feel shame as ashamed people do, and they did not take their disgrace to heart. Therefore they will fall in their destruction, and at the time of their visitation they will perish, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: “Stand at the roads and look, and ask about the Lord’s everlasting paths. See which is the good road, and walk on it, and you will find holiness for your souls.” But they said, “We will not walk on it.”
And I appointed watchmen over you: Listen to the sound of the trumpet. But they say: We will not listen.
Therefore the nations heard, and those who tended the flocks among them.
Listen, earth. Look, I will bring evils upon this people according to the fruit of their rebellion, because they did not heed my words and rejected my law.
Why do you bring me incense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices have not pleased me.
Therefore the Lord says this: Look, I will bring affliction upon this people, and fathers and sons together will be afflicted by it; the neighbor and his companion will perish.
The Lord says this: Look, an army is coming from the north, a great nation; many kings will rise from the ends of the earth.

Archers and spearmen—a brazen and merciless nation. Its voice is like the sound of a surging sea. With chariots and horses it will draw up in battle and [?] like fire in war against you, daughter of Zion.
We have heard the report about them, and our hands have grown weak. Distress has seized us like the labor pains of a woman giving birth.
Do not go out into the fields, and do not travel along the roads, for the sword of the enemies surrounds us.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and spread ashes. Take up mourning for a loved one, and lament with a sorrowful lament, for misery will suddenly come upon us.
I have appointed you as a tester of besieged peoples, and you will learn as I test their ways.
They are all disobedient and walk in stubbornness, like bronze and iron; they are all corrupt.
The bellows have failed from the fire; the lead has run out. The silversmith labors in vain, and their evils have not melted away.
Call them rejected silver, for the Lord has rejected them. Hear the words of the Lord, all Judea.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Stand at the gate of the Lord's house and read these words there, and say: Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah, you who enter through these gates to worship the Lord.
The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says this: Make your ways and your conduct right, and I will let you dwell in this place.
Do not trust the lying words that say, “It is the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord,” for they will not help you at all.
If you truly make your ways and your conduct right, and if you truly carry out justice between a man and his neighbor,
and do not oppress the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers, forever and ever.
But if you put your trust in lying words from which you will gain nothing,
and steal and murder and commit adultery and swear falsely and offer incense to Baal and follow foreign gods whom you do not know, false gods from whom harm will also come to you,
and come and stand before me in this house that bears my name, and say, “We have been kept from committing all those abominations”—
has my house, which bears my name, become a robbers’ cave in your eyes? Look, I too have seen it, says the Lord.
For go to my place in Shiloh, where I first caused my name to dwell, and see what I did to it because of the evils of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these deeds, says the Lord, and I spoke to you morning after morning, but you did not listen to me, and I called you, but you gave me no answer,
I will do to this house that bears my name, in which you put your trust, and to this place that I gave to you and your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
And I will cast you out of my presence, as I cast out your brothers, all the offspring of Ephraim.
And you, do not stand in prayer for this people, and do not seek mercy for them or plead, and do not fall down before me on their behalf, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
Their children gather wood, their fathers light fires, and their women knead dough to make cakes for the hosts of heaven. They offer offerings to foreign gods to provoke me to anger.
Is it me they provoke to anger, says the Lord, and not themselves, bringing shame upon their own faces?

Therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will pour out my anger and my fury upon this place, upon humans and animals, upon the trees of the fields and the produce of the land. It will burn and will not be extinguished.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Gather your burnt offerings together with your sacrifices, and eat the meat.
For I did not speak to your fathers or give them a command concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices on the day when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.
Rather, I gave them this command, saying: Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in all my ways that I commanded you, so that it may go well with you.
But they did not listen to me or incline their ears. Instead, they followed the plans of their evil hearts, and they went backward, not forward.
From the day their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them daily, early in the morning.
But they did not listen to me or incline their ears, and they stiffened their necks more than their fathers did.
You will speak these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You will call them, but they will not answer you.
You will say to them: This is the nation that did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God and did not accept correction. Faithfulness has failed, and truth has been taken from their mouths.
Cut off your hair and throw it away, and take up a lament on your lips, for the Lord has rejected and cast away the generation that did these things.
For the children of Judah have done evil before me, says the Lord. They have set up their abominations in the house that bears my name, to defile it.
They built the altar of Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in fire. I did not command them to do this, nor did it enter my heart.

Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when it will no longer be called the Altar of Topheth or the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom, but the Valley of the Slain. They will bury people in Topheth because there is not enough room.
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to drive them away.

I will remove from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem the sound of celebration and the sound of rejoicing, the voice of the bride and the voice of the bridegroom, for the land will become a wilderness.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring out of their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of their rulers, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

And they will dry them in the sun, under the moon and all the stars, and before all the hosts of heaven, which they loved and served, which they followed and relied upon, and which they worshiped. They will not be mourned or wept over, but will become an object of mockery on the face of the earth.
For they preferred death to life, as did the survivors remaining from that evil nation in all the places where they remain, wherever I banish them, says the Lord of hosts.
You will say to them: Thus says the Lord: Does someone who falls not get up, or someone who turns away not turn back again?
Why, then, has this people, Jerusalem, turned away with such a shameless turning away? They persisted in their own desires and refused to return.
Listen and hear: they do not speak that way, and there is no one who repents of his evils and says, “What have I done?” The runner stopped running, like a horse covered in sweat as it neighs.
Now the stork in the heavens knew its season; the turtledove and the swallow, wild birds, kept the times of their arrival. But my people did not know the judgments of the Lord.
How can you say, “We are wise, and the law of God is among us”? Therefore the scribes’ false allotment has come to nothing.
The wise were put to shame; they were terrified and defeated, because they dishonored the word of the Lord. What wisdom can there be in them?

Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to foreign heirs, because from the least to the greatest of them, everyone greedily pursues gain. From prophet to priest, everyone commits injustice.
They treated the brokenness of the daughter of my people with contempt, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there was no peace.

Will they be ashamed because they committed abomination? Yet even then they felt no shame and took no account of disgrace. Therefore they will fall among the fallen at the time of their visitation, and they will grow weak, says the Lord.
They will gather their produce, says the Lord. There are no grapes in their vineyards and no figs on their fig trees, and the leaf has fallen. I gave to them, and it passed them by.

Now why should we remain seated? Gather together, and let us enter the fortified cities and fall there, for the Lord our God has cast us down and given us bitter water to drink, because we sinned before him.
We gathered in peace, but there was no good; at the time of healing, behold, distress.

From Dan we will hear the sound of his swift horses. At the sound of the neighing of his cavalry, the whole earth shook. He will come and devour the land and all that fills it, the cities and their inhabitants.
For behold, I am sending deadly snakes among you, against which charms have no effect, and they will strike you, says the Lord.
And in the incurable pains of your bewildered hearts

behold, the sound of the lament of the daughter of my people from a distant land: “Is the Lord not in Zion? Is the King not there?” Why did they provoke me to anger with their carved images and their foreign vanities?
The harvests have passed, the summer has passed, and we have not been saved.
Over the brokenness of the daughter of my people, I was broken; I was darkened with bewilderment. Pains like those of a woman in labor overwhelmed me.
Is there no medicine in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why has there been no healing for the daughter of my people?
Oh, that my head were water and my eyes fountains of tears, so that I might weep day and night for this people and for the wounded of the daughter of my people!
If only someone would give me a small lodging in the wilderness, so that I could leave my people and go away from them! For they are all together a company of scoffers.
They bent their tongues like a bow for falsehood, and not for faithfulness; they grew strong upon the earth. For they went from evil to evil and did not know me, says the Lord.
Let each of you beware of his neighbor, and do not trust your brothers, for every brother deceives with deceit, and every friend walks treacherously.
Each mocks his friend, and they do not speak the truth. Their tongues have learned to speak falsehood. They practiced extortion and did not cease piling interest upon interest.
And deceit upon deceit, and they refused to know me, says the Lord.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will heat them in the furnace and test them. What else can I do in the face of the evils of the daughter of my people?
Their deceitful tongues are a wounding arrow. With the words of his mouth, each speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he harbors hostility.
Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall my soul not seek vengeance on such a nation?

Raise a lament over the mountains, and lift your voices in mourning over the hills of the wilderness, for they have dwindled because no people pass through them, and they have not heard the sounds of livestock. From the birds of heaven to the animals, all were bewildered and went away.
I will give Jerusalem over to captivity and make it a dwelling place for dragons, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitants.

Who is the wise man who will understand this? To whom has the word from the Lord’s mouth come, so that he can tell us why the land has perished and been abandoned like a wilderness, with no one passing through?
And the Lord said to me, “Because they abandoned my law, which I set before their eyes, and did not listen to my voice,
but followed the desires of their own evil hearts and the idols that their fathers showed them.”
Therefore the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says this: “Look, I will feed this people calamity and give them bitter water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send a sword against them until I destroy them with it.”
The Lord of hosts says this: “Consider this, and call the mourning women to come. Send for the skilled women, and let them cry out.
Let them hurry and raise a lament over you, so that your eyes shed tears and your eyelids pour out water.
For a mournful voice has sounded from Zion: ‘How miserable we have become! We are deeply ashamed, because we have abandoned the land and cast away our homes.’
Listen, women, to the words of the Lord God, and let your ears receive the words of his mouth. Teach your daughters cries of mourning, and let each woman teach her companion a lament,
for death has climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out the children outside and the young men from the public squares.”
The Lord says this: “Human corpses will lie exposed as a spectacle across the fields of your land, like grass left behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.”
This is what the Lord says: Let the wise man not boast in his wisdom, let the mighty man not boast in his strength, and let the great man not boast in his greatness.

Rather, let those who boast boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the Lord who carries out justice, mercy, and righteousness on the earth. For these are the things I desire, says the Lord.
“Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will punish all who are circumcised in their uncircumcision:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the descendants of Ammon, the descendants of Moab, and all who trim the sides of their faces and live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised in the flesh, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in their hearts.”
Hear the words that the Lord has spoken against you, house of Israel.
The Lord says this: “Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not be terrified by the signs in the heavens, for the nations are afraid of them.
For all the customs of the nations are empty: wood cut from the forest, the work of carpenters’ hands,
adorned with cast silver and gold. They secure them with hammers and nails so that they will not move.

Silver worked on a lathe, silver put to use from Tarshish, and gold brought from Memphath—the hand of a goldsmith has fashioned them, the work of craftsmen. They clothe them in blue and purple. They cannot walk, but must be lifted and carried. They cannot move a foot even one step, nor can they lift themselves to be carried. Do not fear them, for they do no evil, nor is there any good in them.
There is no one like you, Lord. You are great, and your name is great in power.
Who would not fear you, King of the nations? For this is fitting for you. Among all the wise men of the nations and among all their kings, who is like you?
The hearts of the vain will all burn and perish,
for they are wood and choice silver brought from Tarshish, and gold from Sophath, all the work of craftsmen and goldsmiths’ hands. Blue and purple are their clothing, all the work of skilled men.
But the Lord is the true God, the living God and eternal King. At his wrath the earth will shake, and the nations will not endure his anger.
You shall say this to them: “The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”
It is the Lord who made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
When he gives forth his voice, an abundance of waters fills the heavens. He brings up clouds from the ends of the earth, makes his lightning for the rain, and brings the winds out of his storehouses.
Everyone has become foolish in his knowledge; every goldsmith has been put to shame by his carved images, for they have cast falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are worthless and works of deception; at the time of their punishment they will perish.
But the Portion of Jacob is not like this, for the one who created everything is his portion, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The Lord of hosts is his name.
Gather up your possessions from outside, you who dwell among the chosen.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will make the inhabitants of that land stumble through distress, and I will afflict them so that they may not find [?].
Woe over your ruin, for your blows are painful! And I say, “Truly, these are my wounds, and this has come upon me.”

My tent has been ravaged and destroyed, and all my tent curtains have been torn apart. My sons and my flocks are nowhere to be found, and there is no longer a place for my tent or a place for my tent curtains.
For the shepherds became foolish and did not seek the Lord. Therefore they did not understand, and all their grazing animals were scattered.
A voice bringing bad news will come, and a great shaking from the land of the north, to turn the cities of Judah into ruins and dwelling places for ostriches.
I know, Lord, that a person's path is not his own, and no man can walk and make his own paths succeed.
Discipline us, Lord, but with justice and not in anger, so that you do not reduce us to a few.

Pour out your wrath upon the nations that do not know you and upon the peoples that have not called upon your name, for they devoured Jacob, consumed him, and finished him off, and they laid waste his pastures.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Cursed be the person who does not listen to the words of this covenant.

I commanded this to your fathers on the day when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying: Hear my voice and do everything that I command you, and you shall be my people, and I shall be your God.
And I will confirm the oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them the land flowing with honey and milk, as it is today. I answered and said, “Yes, Lord, let it be so.”
And the Lord said to me: Read all these words in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, and say: Hear the message of this covenant and carry it out.
For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians, and until this day, rising early in the mornings and giving warning, saying: Listen to my voice.

But they did not listen and turned their ears away. Each followed the inclination of his own heart toward evil. And I will bring upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to carry out, but they did not.
And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They returned to the wrongdoing of their ancestors of old, who were unwilling to listen to my words. And behold, they follow foreign gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant, which I made with their fathers.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring upon them disasters from which they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
And the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to their gods, to whom they offered incense, but those gods will certainly not save them in the time of their disasters.
For your gods were as numerous as your cities, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s streets you set up shrines and altars of shame to offer incense to Baal.
And you, do not pray for this people, and do not plead for them with petitions and supplication, for I will not listen when they call out to me in the time of their disasters.
For I say concerning the beloved that he has committed abominations inside my temple. Will prayers and consecrated meat take away your evils from you, or will you be saved by such things?
The Lord named you “A beautiful olive tree, leafy in appearance.” At the sound of their pruning, great distress is upon you; your branches have become useless.

And the Lord God of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you in return for the evils of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they committed against themselves, provoking me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
Lord, make it known to me, and I will know. Then I saw their deeds.

Like an innocent lamb led to slaughter, I did not know that they had plotted evil against me, saying, “Come, let us put wood in his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living, so that his name will no longer be remembered.”
Lord of hosts, who judges justly and examines the innermost thoughts and hearts, let me see your vengeance upon them, for I have laid my case before you.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says concerning the men of Anathoth who seek your life and say, “Do not prophesy about us, or you will die by our hands.”
Therefore, this is what the Lord of hosts says: “Look, I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will perish from famine.
No survivors will remain among them, for I will bring disaster upon the inhabitants of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”
You are righteous, Lord, and I will bring my plea before you. Yet I will speak about justice: why do the ways of the wicked prosper, and why do all who act with utter contempt flourish?
You planted them, and they took root; they bore children and produced fruit. You are near in their mouths, Lord, but far from their innermost thoughts.
But you, Lord, know me; you have seen me and tested my heart before you. Gather them like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for the day of slaughter.
How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field dry up? Because of the wickedness of the land’s inhabitants, the animals and birds have perished, for they said, “God will not see our ways.”
Your feet run and wear you out; how will you prepare yourself to run with horses? Now you feel secure in a peaceful land; what will you do when the Jordan River rises?
For even your brothers and your father's household have betrayed you; they have cried out after you and gathered against you. Do not trust them, for they will speak evil of you.
I abandoned my house and left my inheritance. I handed the beloved of my soul over to her enemies.
My inheritance became like a lion in the wilderness to me. She raised her voice against me; therefore I hated her.
Is my inheritance a hyena’s den to me, or are there caves around her? Go around and gather all the wild animals of the wilderness, and let them come to devour her.
Many shepherds ruined my vineyard and destroyed my portion. They turned my desirable inheritance into an untrodden wilderness.
It has been laid waste to destruction. Because of me, the whole land has been utterly laid waste, for there is no one who takes it to heart.
The afflicted passed along every way out of the wilderness, for the sword of the Lord will devour from one end of the earth to the other, and no living being has peace.
Sow wheat, and you will reap thorns, and your portions will bring you no benefit. Be ashamed of your boasts, because of the reproaches before the Lord.

For this is what the Lord says concerning all these evil neighbors who encroach upon my inheritance, which I allotted to my people Israel: “Look, I will uproot them from their own land, and I will bring the house of Judah out from among them.
And after I have uprooted them, I will return and have mercy on them, and settle them, each in his own inheritance and each in his own land.
And if they thoroughly learn the way of my people, swearing by my name, ‘As the Lord lives,’ just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they will be established among my people.
But if they do not turn back, I will wipe out that nation and remove it utterly,” says the Lord.
This is what the Lord said to me: “Go and get yourself a linen loincloth, put it around your waist, and do not pass through water.”
So I got a loincloth according to the Lord’s word and put it around my waist.
The word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying:
“Take the loincloth you bought from around your waist, get up, go to the bank of the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft in the rock.”
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the Lord commanded me.
After many days, the Lord said to me, “Get up, go to the bank of the Euphrates, and take from there the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there.”
So I went to the bank of the Euphrates River, dug, and took the loincloth from the place where I had buried it. And look, the loincloth was ruined; it was no longer useful for anything.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Thus says the Lord: In this way I will destroy the pride of Judah and the pride of Jerusalem.

My city and my wicked people, who refused to listen to my words, who follow the inclinations of their evil hearts and go after foreign gods to serve them and worship them, will become like that belt, which is good for nothing.

For just as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, says the Lord, to be my renowned people, my boast and my glory. But they did not listen to me.

And you shall speak this message to this people: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Every wineskin shall be filled with wine. And if they say to you, Do we not know very well that every wineskin shall be filled with wine?

You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Look, I am filling all the inhabitants of this land, the kings who are sons of David and sit on his throne, the priests, the prophets, Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with drunkenness.
I will scatter them, each man and his brother, fathers and their sons together, says the Lord. I will have no pity, nor spare them, nor show mercy when I destroy them.
Hear and pay attention, and do not be proud, for the Lord has spoken.
Give glory to the Lord your God before darkness falls and your feet stumble on the dark mountains. You will look for light, but there will be the shadows of death, and you will be left in darkness.
If you do not listen to him, your souls will weep in secret because of your enemies. You will be filled with tears, and your eyes will shed tears, because the Lord's flock has been crushed.
Say to the king and the rulers: Bow down and sit, for your glorious crown has fallen from your heads.
The cities in the south were shut, and there was no one to open them. Judah was taken captive in a final captivity, the full repayment.
Lift up your eyes, Jerusalem, and see those sent from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your glorious sheep?
What answer will you give when they call you to account? You yourself taught them how to rule over you. Will not labor pains seize you like a woman giving birth?
If you say in your heart, 'Why has this happened to me?' it is because of your great wickedness that your rear has been exposed and your heels disgraced.
If an Ethiopian can change his skin, or a leopard its spots, then you too can do good, though you have learned to do evil.
I will scatter them like straw driven by the wind in the wilderness.
That is your lot and your portion for not trusting me [?], because you forgot me and trusted in lies.
I myself will uncover your skirts and throw them over your head and face, and your shame will be seen.

I have seen your adultery and your neighing, your estrangement from me through your prostitution, and your abominations at the altars and in the fields. Woe to you, Jerusalem, for you will not become clean by following me! How long will this continue with you?
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah concerning the lack of rain.
Mourning seized Judea, and its gates became deserted. They grew dark upon the earth, and Jerusalem's cry rose up.
Their nobles sent their young men for water. They came to the wells and found no water. They brought their vessels back empty; they were ashamed and humiliated, and covered their heads.
The work of the land failed because there was no rain upon the earth. The farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
The deer gave birth in the open country and abandoned their young because there was no vegetation.
The wild donkeys in the fields sucked in air like dragons, and their eyes wasted away because there was no grass.
Though our sins stand against us, act, Lord, for the sake of your name, for our sins before you are many. We have sinned against you.
Hope of Israel, Lord, save us in times of trouble. Why have you become like a stranger in the land, or like a resident of the land who turns aside to lodgings?
Are you like a man who sleeps, or like a man who cannot save? Yet you are among us, Lord, and your name is called over us. Do not forget us.

This is what the Lord says to this people: They have loved to move their feet in this way and have not restrained them, and God has not been pleased with them. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish their sins.
And the Lord said to me: Do not pray for the welfare of that people.
For even if they fast, I will not hear their petitions, and if they offer burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not be pleased with them, for I will destroy them by sword, famine, and death.

And I said: O you who are, Lord, Lord! Look, the prophets tell them, ‘You will not see the sword, and there will be no famine among you, for I will grant truth and peace upon the land and in this place.’

And the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy lies in my name. I did not send them, did not command them, and did not speak to them. They prophesy to you false visions, wishes, divinations, and the desires of their own hearts.

Therefore this is what the Lord says about the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I did not send them or command them, and who say, ‘There will be no sword or famine in this land’: Those prophets will perish from a wasting, deadly disease, by sword, and by famine.

And the people to whom they prophesy will lie cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of the sword and famine. There will be no one to bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. And I will pour their own evils upon them.

And you shall say this word to them: Let tears flow from your eyes day and night, and do not let them cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been broken with a great fracture and with exceedingly painful blows.
If I go out into the field, there are those wounded by the sword; and if I enter the city, there are the sufferings of famine. For prophet and priest have gone to a land they did not know.

Have you utterly rejected Judah, or has your soul completely withdrawn? Why have you struck us, so that there is no healing for us? We looked for peace, but there was no good; for a time of healing, but there was turmoil.
We acknowledge, Lord, our sins and the wrongdoing of our fathers, for we have sinned before you.
For your name's sake, stop; do not destroy the throne of your glory. Remember; do not break your covenant with us.
Is there any among the idols of the nations who can make it rain? Or can the heavens give their abundance? Are you not the one, Lord our God? We will wait for you, for you made all these things.
And the Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not be with them. Send this people away from my presence, and let them go out.

And if they say to you, ‘Where shall we go?’ you shall say to them: This is what the Lord says: Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; and those destined for captivity, to captivity.
And I will exact vengeance from them in four ways, says the Lord: the sword to kill, dogs to tear apart, and the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
And I will hand them over to danger among all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and because of everything he did in Jerusalem.
Who will pity you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn over you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?
For you turned away from me, says the Lord, and you will go backward. I will stretch out my hand against you and destroy you, and I will no longer heed them.
And I will scatter them abroad at the gates of my people. They became childless, for I destroyed my people because of their evils, and they did not turn back.

Because of me, their widows became more numerous than the sand of the sea. I brought young men against them and against the mother as enemies at noon. I cast [?], and trembling and distress came suddenly.

The woman who bore seven children has been left empty; her soul has grown weary. Her sun has set at midday; she has been put to shame and disgraced. I will give their survivors to the sword before their enemies, says the Lord.

Woe to me, my mother! What sort of man have you borne in me—a man subjected to disputes and dragged into court throughout the whole land? I owe nothing, and no one owes me anything, yet my strength has failed because of those who curse me.
May it be so, Lord, and may things go well for them! Did I not stand before you in the time of their troubles and in the time of their distress, for their good against the enemy?
Will iron and a bronze wall—your strength—be recognized?
And I will give your treasures to foreigners as a ransom because of all your sins throughout all your territory.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled by my anger; it will blaze against you.

You know, Lord. Remember me, Lord, and visit me. Clear me of blame before my persecutors, and do not delay on my account. Know how much reproach I have borne for your sake from those who despise your words.
Bring them to an end, and let your word become joy and gladness for my heart, for your name has been called over me, Lord God Almighty.
I did not sit in the assembly of mockers, but I trembled before your hand. I sat alone, for I was filled with bitterness.
Why do those who distress me grow strong, and why are my wounds severe? How shall I be healed? You have indeed become to me like cold water that cannot be trusted.

Therefore the Lord says: If you return here, I will shelter you, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be like my mouth. They may turn to you, but you must no longer turn to them.
I will make you a strong bronze wall against this people. They will fight against you, but they will not be able to overcome you, for I am with you to save and deliver you, says the Lord.
I will rescue you from the hands of the wicked and deliver you from the hands of the cruel, says the Lord God of Israel.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
You must not take a wife, and you must not have sons or daughters born to you in this place.
For the Lord says this concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bear them and their fathers who beget them in this land:

They will die of a wasting disease. They will not be mourned or buried, but will lie exposed in disgrace on the face of the earth. They will fall by the sword and perish from famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

The Lord says: Do not enter their mourning, do not go to their lamentation, and do not mourn for them, for I have taken away my peace from that people, says the Lord, as well as my mercy and compassion.
The great and the small will die in that land. They will not be mourned; people will not cut themselves or shave themselves for them, nor will they weep for them or bury them.
No bread of mourning will be broken for them to comfort them over the dead, and they will not be given the cup of consolation over their father or mother.
Do not enter a house of drinking to sit with them, eat, and drink.

For the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will put an end in this place, before your eyes and in your own days, to the sound of gladness and the sound of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

And when you tell that people all these messages, they will say to you: Why has the Lord pronounced all these great disasters against us? What wrongdoing is there among us, or what sin have we committed before the Lord our God?
And you shall say to them, “Because your fathers abandoned me, says the Lord, and followed foreign gods, served them, and worshiped them; they abandoned me and did not keep my law.”
“And you have acted more foolishly than your fathers. Look, each of you follows the desires of your own evil heart, refusing to listen to me.”
And I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known. There you shall serve foreign gods day and night, and they will show you no mercy.
Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when they will no longer say: As the Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

But rather, “As the Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel up from the land of the north and from all the countries where they had been driven.” And he will settle them again in their own land, which he gave to their fathers.

“Look, I am sending many fishermen, says the Lord, and they will catch them. After that I will send many hunters, and they will hunt them on every mountain and every hill, and out of the crevices of the rocks.”
“For my eyes are on all their ways. They have not hidden from my presence, nor have their injustices been concealed from my eyes.”

“And first I will repay them double for their injustices and their sins, with which they defiled my land—with the carcasses of their detestable things and with their lawless deeds, with which they filled my inheritance.”
Lord, my strength, my help, and my refuge in the day of trouble, nations will come to you from the ends of the earth and say, “How falsely our fathers made idols, and there was no benefit in them!”
Can a person make gods for himself, when they are not gods?
“Therefore, look, at this time I will show them; I will make my hand and my power known to them, and they will know that my name is the Lord.”
The sins of Judah are written with an iron pen, with a diamond stylus. They are fixed on the tablets of their hearts and on the horns of your altars,
when their children remember their altars and their sacred groves upon the leafy trees and upon the high hills.
And on the mountains of the countryside I will give your strength and all your treasures as plunder, and your high places, because of sins throughout all your borders.

“And [?], and you will be brought low, deprived of your inheritance, which I gave you. I will deliver you into the hands of your enemies in a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled in my anger; it will blaze forever.”
Thus says the Lord: “Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human being, relies on the flesh of that person's arm, and whose heart turns away from the Lord.”
“He will be like a wild bramble in the wilderness and will not see when good comes. He will live in the salty places of the wilderness, in a salt land where no one ever lives.”
“Blessed is the person who trusts in the Lord, and whose hope is the Lord.”

“He will be like a flourishing tree beside streams of water, spreading its roots along the streams. He will not fear when heat comes, and his branches will grow thickly around him. In a year of drought he will not fear, nor will he cease to bear fruit.”
The heart is deeper than all things, and it is human; who can know it?
“I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each person according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.”
A partridge calls out and gathers what it did not hatch. So is the person who gathers wealth unjustly: in the middle of his days he will leave it, and at his end he will be a fool.
A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
Lord, the hope of Israel, all who abandon you will be put to shame. Those who turn away will be written in the earth, because they abandoned the Lord, the spring of living water.
Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed. Save me, Lord, and I will be saved, for you are my boast.
Look, they say to me, “Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come here!”
But I will not grow weary of following you, and I have not desired the day of man. You yourself know: whatever comes from my lips is before your face.
Do not be a stranger to me; spare me on the day of trouble.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be ashamed. Let them be terrified, but do not let me be terrified. Bring a day of disaster upon them; crush them with a double crushing.
Thus the Lord says to me: Go and stand at the gates of your people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
And you shall say to them: Hear the words of the Lord, kings of Judah, all Judea, and all you inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter through these gates.
Thus says the Lord: Watch yourselves, and do not carry burdens on the Sabbath day or go out through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not bring burdens out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do not do any work. Keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
But they did not listen or incline their ears. They stiffened their necks more than their fathers, refusing to listen to me or accept instruction.
And if you truly listen to me, says the Lord, bringing no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keeping the Sabbath day holy by doing no work on it.

Kings and rulers who sit on David’s throne shall enter through the gates of this city, riding in their chariots and on their horses, together with their rulers, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And this city shall be inhabited forever.

They shall come from the cities of Judah around Jerusalem, from Benjamin, from the plains, from the hill country, and from the southern regions, bringing burnt offerings, incense, manna, and frankincense, offering praise in the house of the Lord.

But if you do not listen to me and keep the Sabbath day holy by not carrying burdens and entering through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, I will kindle a fire in its gates. It shall consume everything around Jerusalem and shall not be extinguished.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Arise, go down to the potter’s house, and there you shall hear my words.
I went down to the potter’s house, and there he was, working on the stones.
A vessel that he was making from clay fell from his hands, and he made it again into another vessel, as it pleased him to make it.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Can I not do with you as this potter does, house of Israel? says the Lord. Behold, as clay is in the potter's hands, so you are in my hands, house of Israel.
If I make a final pronouncement concerning a nation or kingdom, to uproot, tear down, and destroy them,
and that nation turns from its wickedness, concerning which I spoke against them, I too will relent concerning the disaster that I planned to bring upon them.
And if I make a final pronouncement concerning a nation and kingdom, to build and plant,
and they do evil before me by not listening to my voice, I too will relent concerning the good that I said I would do for them.

Now speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and say: Thus says the Lord: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Now let each of you turn from his evil way, and set your conduct and your ways straight.
But they say: We will take courage! We will follow our rebellions, and each of us will do what pleases his evil heart.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Now, please inquire among the nations: Who has heard of such terrible things as the virgin Israel has done in such excess?
Will breasts fail from a rock, or snow from Lebanon? Or will waters be forcibly turned back by the violence of the wind?
For my people have forgotten me; they have offered incense in vain. They shall falter in their ways, in their ancient allotted lands, turning onto paths where there is no road to travel,
making their land a ruin and an object of hissing forever. Everyone who passes through it shall be astonished and shake his head.
Like a scorching wind, I will scatter them before their enemies. I will show them my back and not my face on the day of their destruction.

And they said, “Come, let us devise a plan against Jeremiah, for the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor a word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with our tongues and pay no attention to any of his words.”
Hear me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my plea.
Should evil be repaid for good? For they spoke together against my life and concealed their torments. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your anger away from them.

Therefore, give their children over to famine and gather them into the power of the sword. Let their wives be childless and widowed, and let their men be struck down by death and their young men fall by the sword in battle.
Let a cry of distress arise in their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them, for they put their words into action to seize me and hid snares for me.

And you, Lord, know all their plans to put me to death. Do not forgive their wrongdoing, and do not erase their sins from before your face. Let sickness come upon them before you; act against them in the time of your anger.
Then the Lord said to me, “Go and buy yourself a jar made of clay, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.
Go out to the burial grounds of their sons, which are before the entrance of the Harsith Gate, and proclaim there all the words that I will speak to you.

Say to them, ‘Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah, men of Judea, and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will bring disaster upon this place, so that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring,

because they abandoned me and alienated this place from me. They burned incense here to foreign gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah knew, and they filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They built altars to Baal to burn their sons in fire as burnt offerings to Baal, something I did not command or speak of, nor did it enter my heart.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when this place will no longer be called Ruin or the Burial Ground of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

I will frustrate the counsel of Judah and the counsel of Jerusalem in that place. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and into the hands of those who seek their lives. I will give their corpses as food to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth.
I will make that city a ruin and an object of hissing. Everyone who passes through it will grieve and hiss at all its wounds.

They will eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each will eat the flesh of a companion, in the distress and siege with which their enemies and those who seek their lives will besiege them.’”
“Break the jar before the men who go out with you,

and say to them, ‘This is what the Lord of hosts says to me: In this way I will break this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is broken and cannot be repaired again. They will bury people in Topheth because there is no room for burial.
Thus will I do to this place, says the Lord, and to its inhabitants, reducing this city to ruins.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be like the place of the slain because of the defilements they committed in all the houses where they burned incense on their rooftops to all the host of heaven and presented offerings to foreign gods.’”
Jeremiah came from the ruined place of Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy. He stood in the courtyard of the Lord’s house and said to all the people:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am bringing upon this city and all its cities and villages every disaster that I spoke of against it, because they stiffened their necks and would not listen to my words.
Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was the commander and chief officer in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and confined him in the upper stocks at the Gate of Benjamin, in the upper chamber in the house of the Lord.
And the next morning Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has not called your name Pashhur, but Wandering Captive.

For thus says the Lord: Look, I will give you over to captivity, together with all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies, and your eyes will see it. I will deliver you and your whole house of Judah into the hands of the king of Babylon. They will take them captive to Babylon and slaughter them with the sword.

I will deliver all the resources of this city, all its labor, all its splendor, and all the treasures of your king of Judah into the hands of their enemies. They will plunder them, seize them, and carry them to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied lies.
You deceived me, Lord, and I was deceived. You overpowered me and prevailed. I became a laughingstock all day long; I was utterly ridiculed.
For with the bitterness of my words I will mock contempt, and because of misery I will raise a cry. For the word of the Lord has become a source of reproach and ridicule for me every day.

And I said, “I will not mention the Lord’s name or speak in his name anymore.” But in my heart it became like a burning fire blazing through my bones. I grew weary on every side, and I cannot keep quiet.

For I heard the accusations of many who had gathered together around me: “Come, let us rise against him!” All the men who are his friends say, “Devise schemes against him. Perhaps he will be deceived, and we will overcome him and take our revenge on him.”

But the Lord was with me like a warrior and gave me strength. Therefore they persecuted me, but they could not understand the schemes. They were greatly ashamed because they understood nothing. May their everlasting disgrace never be forgotten.
Lord of hosts, you who weigh justice and examine hearts and kidneys, let me see your vengeance upon them, for I have made my plea known to you.
Bless the Lord; praise him, for he has rescued the life of the poor from the hands of the wicked.
Cursed be the day on which I was born! Let the day on which my mother bore me not be commemorated.
Cursed be the man who brought good news to my father, saying, “A male child has been born to you,” and made him rejoice greatly.
Let that man be like the cities that the Lord overthrew in anger without relenting. Let him hear bad news in the morning and an outcry at noon.
For he did not kill me there in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and her womb would have remained pregnant forever.
Why did this happen to me—that I came out of the womb to see pain and toil, and my days ended in shame?
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to him, saying:
“Inquire of the Lord for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has come against us. Perhaps the Lord will act on our behalf according to all his wonders and turn him away from us.”
Jeremiah said to them, “Say this to Zedekiah:

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Look, I am turning back the weapons of war that you hold in your hands, with which you fight against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the walls. I will gather them into the midst of this city.
I myself will wage war against you with an uplifted hand and a raised arm, in anger, fury, and great wrath.
And I will strike all the inhabitants of that city, both people and animals, with a great plague, and they will die.

And after that, this is what the Lord says: I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, and the people who remain in that city after surviving death, the sword, and famine, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hands of their enemies, and into the hands of those who seek their lives. They will strike them down with the sword, and I will not spare them, show them mercy, or have compassion on them.
And you shall say to the people: This is what the Lord says: Look, I have set before you the way of life and the way of death.

Whoever stays in that city will die by the sword, famine, and death. But whoever goes out and presents himself to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live. His life will be his reward, and he will live.
For I have set my face against that city for harm and not for good, says the Lord. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
House of the king of Judah and house of David, hear the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord says:

Administer justice in the morning and uphold people's rights. Rescue those who have been robbed from the hands of their oppressors, so that my anger does not flare up like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it because of the injustice of your conduct.
Look, I am against you who dwell in the ravines of the plain of Tyre, says the Lord, you who said, “Who will frighten us, or who will enter our dwellings?”
And I will punish you according to the wickedness of your conduct, says the Lord. I will kindle a fire in its forests, and it will consume everything around it.
This is what the Lord says: Go, descend to the house of the king of Judah, speak this word there, and say:
Hear the word of the Lord, king of Judah who sits on David's throne—you, your servants, and your people who enter through these gates.

This is what the Lord says: Practice justice and righteousness. Rescue those who have been robbed from the hands of their oppressors. Do not oppress the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and do not act wickedly. Do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you truly carry out this command, kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this house and ride in chariots and on horses, the king himself, his servants, and his people.
But if you do not carry out these commands, I swear by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a ruin.
