For this is what the Lord says concerning the house of the king of Judah: You are Gilead to me, the summit of Lebanon. Yet I will surely make you a ruin, cities without inhabitants.
And I will bring destroyers against you, each man with his axe. They will cut down your choicest cedars and throw them into the fire.
And many nations will pass through that city, and each person will say to his companion, “Why has the Lord done this to this great city?”
And they will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down to foreign gods, and served them.”
Do not weep for the dead or mourn him. Instead, weep bitterly for the one who goes away and will never return or see the land of his birth.
For this is what the Lord says concerning Shallum son of Josiah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah, who departed from this place and will never return there:
For he will die in the place where they took him captive, and he will never see this land again.
Woe to the one who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his neighbor work for him for nothing and does not pay him his wages.
For you built yourself a well-proportioned house, a cool upper room fitted with windows, paneled with cedar and coated with naphtha.
Will you reign because you became enraged in your father's cedar-built houses? Let them neither eat nor drink, for they did not know justice, righteousness, or goodness.
And they did not uphold the rights of the needy or give justice to the poor. Is this not precisely what it means not to know me? says the Lord.
Look, neither your eyes nor your heart are set on goodness, but on greed, on shedding innocent blood, on injustice, and on committing murder.

Therefore the Lord says this concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They shall not mourn for this man or say, “Alas, alas, brother! Alas, alas, brother!” They shall not mourn and say, “Alas, alas, lord! Alas, alas, beloved!”
He shall be buried with a donkey’s burial; he shall be thrown out, rotting, outside the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out, and raise your voice in Bashan. Raise a cry beyond the sea, for all your lovers have been shattered together.
I spoke to you when you went astray, and you said, “I will not listen to you.” This has been your way since your youth, for you have not listened to my voice.
The winds shall shepherd all your shepherds, and all your lovers shall go into captivity. Then you shall be ashamed and dishonored by all your loved ones.
You who dwell in Lebanon, who are fortified among the cedars, shall groan when pains and labor come upon you, like a woman giving birth.
As I live, says the Lord, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, should become a signet on his right hand, even from there I will tear you away.

And I will deliver you into the hands of those seeking your life, and into the hands of those whose faces you feared, and into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, and into the hands of the Chaldeans.
And I will cast you and your mother into a foreign land where you have never gone, and there you shall die.
And to this land, to which they pledge in their souls to return, they shall not return.
For he himself fell, along with his offspring, and became an exile, a despised mouth [?], shaken off. The man Jeconiah was dishonored like a useless vessel; he fell into a land he did not know.
Earth, earth, earth, hear the words of the Lord!
The Lord says this: Record this man as an exile, for he shall not prosper in his days, nor shall any man among his offspring prosper who sits on David’s throne as ruler of the house of Judah.
Woe to the shepherds who destroyed and scattered the sheep of your pasture, says the Lord.

Therefore the Lord, the God of Israel, says this concerning the shepherds who shepherd my people: You scattered my sheep and drove them away, and you did not care for them. Now, behold, I will exact vengeance from you according to the evil of your deeds, says the Lord.
And I will gather the remnant of my people from every land where I drove them, and I will establish them in their pastures. They shall increase and multiply.
And I will raise up shepherds who shall shepherd them, and they shall no longer be afraid or terrified, nor shall they be neglected, says the Lord.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will raise up for David a Branch of righteousness. A king shall reign and act wisely, and he shall administer justice and righteousness on the earth.
In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell in hope. And this is his name, which the Lord shall call him: “Jozadak among the prophets, our righteousness.”
Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when they shall no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the house of Israel out of the land of the Egyptians,”
but rather, “As the Lord lives, who brought all the offspring of Israel out of the northern land and out of all the countries where he had driven them, and sheltered them again in their own land.”

Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me; all my bones tremble. I have become like a shattered man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the Lord and because of the majesty of his glory.
For the land is full of adulterers; because of the oath the land mourned, and the pastures of the wilderness dried up. Their course has become evil, and their strength is not right.
For prophet and priest have been defiled, and even in my house I have found their wickedness, says the Lord.
Therefore their path will become a stumbling block to them. In the mist they will stumble and fall on it, for I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their visitation, says the Lord.
Among the prophets of Samaria I saw lawlessness, for they prophesied through Baal and led my people Israel astray.

Among the prophets of Jerusalem I saw horrible things, for they committed adultery, followed lies, and strengthened the hands of evildoers, so that no one turned from his evil way. To me they have all become like Sodom, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts says concerning the prophets: Look, I will feed them suffering and give them bitter water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem defilement has spread throughout the whole land.

This is what the Lord of hosts says: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you, for they fill you with empty talk. They speak visions from their own hearts, not from the mouth of the Lord.

They say to those who rebel against the word of the Lord, ‘You will have peace.’ And to all who follow their own desires, and to everyone who follows the error of his own heart, they say, ‘No disaster will come upon you.’
For who has stood in the council of the Lord and seen and heard his word? Who has paid attention to my word and heard it?
Look, a shaking comes from the Lord, and wrath will burst out upon the ungodly with a stormy shaking.
The Lord’s anger will come and will not turn back until he has accomplished and established the purpose of his heart. In the last days they will understand it clearly.
I did not send the prophets, yet they ran. I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
If he had stood in my council, he would have made my people hear my words and turned them from their evil ways and their evil conduct.
Am I a God nearby, says the Lord, and not a God far away?
Can a person hide in a hiding place without my seeing him? says the Lord. Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord.
I heard what the prophets said, who prophesied lies in my name and said, ‘I had a dream.’
How long will this be in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy lies and prophesy the desires of their own hearts?
They plan to make my people forget my laws through their dreams, which each tells to his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot my name through Baal.
Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, and let the one who has my word speak my word truthfully. What has straw to do with wheat? says the Lord.
Are not my words like fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
Therefore, look, I am against these prophets, says the Lord, who steal my words, each from his neighbor.
Look, I am against these prophets, says the Lord, who reject the prophets with their tongue and slumber in their own slumbers.

Look, I am against these prophets who prophesy lying dreams, says the Lord, and tell them and lead my people astray through their lies and their errors. I did not send them or command them, and they will bring no benefit at all to this people, says the Lord.
If this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, ‘What is the burden of the Lord?’ you shall say to them, ‘You are the burden, and I will cast you down, says the Lord.’
As for the prophet, priest, or person who says, ‘The burden of the Lord,’ I will exact vengeance upon that person and his household.
Why do you not instead say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother, ‘What answer has the Lord given, and what has the Lord spoken?’
Do not mention ‘the burden of the Lord’ anymore, for each person’s own word will be the burden of the Lord, and you will distort the words of the living God, the Lord of hosts, our God.
Instead, you shall say this to the prophet: ‘What answer has the Lord given you, and what has the Lord spoken?’

If you say, “The burden of the Lord,” this is what the Lord says about it: “Because you have said these words, ‘The burden of the Lord,’ and I did not send word to you saying, ‘Do not say, “The burden of the Lord,”’
therefore, look, I will lift you up and destroy you and the city that I gave you and your ancestors, removing you from my presence.
And I will bring everlasting reproach and everlasting disgrace upon you, which will not be forgotten.”

And the Lord showed me two baskets of figs standing before the Lord’s temple, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, the locksmiths, and the nobles from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
One basket contained very sweet figs, like early-ripening figs, and the second basket contained foul-tasting figs that could not be eaten because they were so bad.
And the Lord said to me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” And I said, “Figs: sweet figs, very sweet, and bad figs, very bad, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad.”
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says:
‘Like these sweet figs, so I have regarded for good the exiles of Judah whom I sent from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set my eyes upon them for good and give them refuge in this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
And I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord. They will be my people, and I will be their God, because they will return to me with all their heart.

And like these rotten figs, which cannot be eaten because of their rottenness’—this is what the Lord says—‘so I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his leading men, the remnant of Jerusalem, the remnant of this land, and those living in Egypt.
I will scatter them throughout all the kingdoms of the earth and make them a reproach, a proverb, an object of hatred, and a curse in every place where I drive them.
And I will send sword, famine, and death against them until they have vanished from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.’”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. That year was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

“From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until today—these twenty-three years—the word of the Lord has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising early in the mornings and speaking, but you have not listened.
And I sent my servants the prophets to you, sending them early in the mornings, but you did not listen or incline your ears to hear.
I said, ‘Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from your evil conduct, and dwell in the land that I gave you and your ancestors from of old and forever.
Do not follow foreign gods to serve them and worship them, and do not provoke me with the works of your hands, causing me to afflict you.’
‘But you did not listen to me,’ says the Lord, ‘and so you provoke me with the works of your hands, causing me to afflict you.’
Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts says: ‘Because you have not believed my words,

look, I will send for and gather all the nations of the north,’ says the Lord, ‘and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I will bring them against this land, against its inhabitants, and against all the nations around it. I will devastate them and make them an object of destruction, of hissing, and of everlasting reproach.
And I will make the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstone and the light of the lamp disappear from among them.
And this whole land will become a ruin and a wasteland, and they will serve those nations and the king of Babylon for seventy years.

And when the seventy years are completed, I will exact retribution from the king of Babylon and from that nation,’ says the Lord, ‘for their lawless deeds, and from the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make them an everlasting desolation.
And I will bring upon that entire land all my words that I spoke concerning it, according to everything written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
For they served among them, since they too are many nations and great kingdoms. And I will repay them according to their lawlessness and according to the works of their hands.’”
For this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says to me: “Take this cup of unmixed wine from my hands, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.”
“They will drink and drain it and go mad because of the sword that I will send among them.”
And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and made all the nations to whom the Lord sent me drink it:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its rulers, to make them a ruin and a wilderness, an object of hissing and a curse, as they are this day;
and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, his servants, his nobles, and all his people;
and all his forces, all the kings of the island, and all the kings of the land of the Philistines: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
and Edom, the Moabites, and the Ammonites;
and all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of the Sidonians, and the kings of the island beyond the sea;
and Dedan, Teman, Buz [?], and all who clip the hair at the sides of their faces;
and all the kings of the Arabs, and all the kings of the mixed peoples dwelling in the wilderness;
And all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Persia.
and all the kings of the north and the east, near and far, each with his brother, and all the kings of the earth who are on the face of the earth. And the king of Sheshach will drink after them all.

And you shall say to them: “This is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Drink and become drunk, act like fools, fall, and do not rise again, because of the sword that I will send among you.”
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, you shall say to them: “This is what the Lord of hosts says: You shall certainly drink!”

“For look, I will begin to inflict suffering on the city that bears my name, and will you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I will summon a sword against everyone who lives on the earth,” says the Lord of hosts.

And you shall prophesy all these words against them and say to them: “The Lord will issue a command from on high, from his holy place. He will raise his voice, a word of command from his dwelling, and they will answer like harvesters over all the inhabitants of the earth, saying, ‘Destruction has come from the edge of the earth.’”
For the Lord has a judgment among the nations, and he himself will judge all flesh. The ungodly have been handed over to the sword, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord of hosts says: “Look, disasters are coming from nation to nation, and a great storm will rise from the ends of the earth.”

And on the day of the Lord, those wounded by the Lord will lie from one end of the earth to the other. They shall not be mourned or gathered; they will be cast down like dung on the surface of the open country.
Wail, shepherds, and cry out! Mourn, rams of the flock, for your days have run their course for your slaughter and scattering. You will fall like choice rams.
And escape will vanish for the shepherds, and deliverance for the rams of the flock.
The sound of the shepherds’ lament and the cry of the rams of the flock, for the Lord has destroyed their pastures.
And the beauty of peace will cease before the Lord’s anger and fury.
They left their thicket like a lion, and their land became a wilderness because of the anger and fury of the great sword and because of his anger and fury.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the Lord, saying:

“This is what the Lord says: Stand in the court of the Lord’s house, and prophesy to all the house of Judah who come to worship in the Lord’s house all the words that I instructed you to prophesy to them. Do not leave out any of these words.”
Perhaps they will listen and each turn from his evil way, and I will relent from the disaster I plan to bring upon them because of their evil deeds.
And you shall say to them, “Thus says the Lord: If you do not listen to me and walk according to my law, which I set before you,
and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I sent to you early and sent again, though you did not listen—”
And I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.
The priests, the false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord.
When Jeremiah finished speaking everything that the Lord had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the false prophets, and all the people seized him and said, “You must die!

Why have you prophesied in the name of the Lord and said, ‘This house will become like Shiloh, and this city will be laid waste, without inhabitants’?” And the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
The officials of Judah heard these words and went up from the king’s house to the house of the Lord, and they sat at the entrance of the Lord’s new gate.
And the priests and the false prophets said to the officials and to all the people, “This man deserves a sentence of death, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears.”
Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, “The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the words that you have heard.
Now set your ways and your deeds right, and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will relent from the disaster he has pronounced against you.
As for me, here I am in your hands. Do with me whatever seems good and right to you.

But know for certain that if you kill me, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its inhabitants, for the Lord truly sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.”
The officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, “This man does not deserve a death sentence, for he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord God.”
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of the people,

“Micah the Moreshethite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He spoke to all the people of Judah and said, ‘Thus says the Lord of hosts: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become like the huts of fruit-watchmen, and the mountain of the house will become like a wooded forest.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did they not fear the Lord and seek the Lord’s favor? And the Lord relented from all the disaster he had pronounced against them. But we have brought great evils upon ourselves.”
There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the Lord, Uriah son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in keeping with all the words of Jeremiah.
And King Jehoiakim, all his warriors, and all his officials heard all his words, and they sought to kill him. When Uriah heard this, he was afraid and fled and went to the land of Egypt.
King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor, and men with him, to Egypt.
They brought him out of there and took him to King Jehoiakim, who killed him with the sword and threw him into the burial place of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so that he was not handed over to the people to be killed.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Thus the Lord said to me: “Make yourself bonds and yokes, and put them around your neck.
Send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre, and the king of the Sidonians, through their messengers who come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to say to their masters, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: This is what you shall say to your masters:
I made the earth, the people, the animals, and everything on the face of the earth by my great power and my own uplifted arm, and I will give it to whomever pleases me.
And now I have given all the earth into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, my servant. I have even given him the wild animals of the wilderness to put to work in his service.
All nations shall serve him, his son, and his grandson, until the time of wrath against his land comes; and many nations and great kings shall serve him.

And any nation or kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon—I will punish that nation with sword, famine, and death, says the LORD, until they are destroyed by his hand.
Do not listen to your prophets, your desires, your dreams, your diviners, your interpreters of bird omens, or your sorcerers, who tell you, ‘You shall not pay tribute to the king of Babylon.’
For they prophesy lies to you to remove you from your land; and I will scatter you, and you will perish.
But the nation that puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and pays tribute to him—I will leave it in its own land, says the LORD, and it shall cultivate it and live in it.
And I spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah, according to all these words, saying: Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and you will live.
Why should you and your people die by sword, famine, and death, as the LORD has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who tell you, ‘Do not pay tribute to the king of Babylon.’ They prophesy falsely to you.
For I did not send them, says the LORD, yet they prophesy lies in my name to destroy you. You will perish, both you and the prophets who prophesy to you falsely and without warrant.

And to the priests and all the people to whom I spoke, you shall say: Thus says the LORD: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you and say, ‘Look, the furnishings of the LORD’s house will now soon return from Babylon.’ They prophesy falsely to you, and I did not send them.
Do not listen to them, but serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

If they are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them come and stand before me. For thus says the LORD: The remaining furnishings, which the king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah captive from Jerusalem to Babylon, shall go, says the LORD of hosts. But concerning the remaining furnishings in the LORD’s house and in the house of the king of Judah not going from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Thus says the LORD of hosts concerning the pillars, the Sea, the stands, and the remaining furnishings that were left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, did not take when he carried Jeconiah, son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, captive from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem:
Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the furnishings remaining in the LORD’s house, in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
They shall go to Babylon and remain there until the day when I attend to them. Thus says the LORD: I will bring them out and return them to this place.

In that year, at the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the Lord, before the priests and all the people.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: The yoke of the king of Babylon will be broken.
After another two full years, I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the Lord’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.

And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the captives of Judah who went to Babylon, I will bring back to this place, says the Lord—Jeconiah and the captives of Judah—for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Hananiah the false prophet before the priests and before all the people who were standing in the house of the Lord.
Indeed, may the Lord do so! May the Lord confirm the words you have prophesied, bringing back the vessels of this house and all the captives from Babylon to this place.
But listen to the message of the Lord that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all these people.
The prophets who were before me and you from ancient times prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms concerning war, disasters, and death.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when the prophet’s word comes true, they will know that this is a prophet whom the Lord has truly sent to them.
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke-bands from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet before all the people and broke them.

Hananiah said before all the people, “Thus says the Lord: In this same way, within two full years I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of every nation.” And Jeremiah the prophet went on his way.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke-bands from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
Go, speak to Hananiah and say, “Thus says the Lord: You have broken wooden yokes, and I will make iron yokes in their place.”

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have placed an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, so that they must pay tribute to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I have also given him the wild animals of the wilderness.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, “Now listen, Hananiah: the Lord did not send you, and you have vainly led this people to put their hope in falsehoods.”
Therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will remove you from the face of the earth, and you will die this very year, because you have spoken rebellion against the Lord.
And Hananiah the prophet died that year, in the seventh month.

These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders of the exiles, to the priests, and to the false prophets. Letter to Babylon, to the exiles and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had taken captive from Jerusalem to Babylon.
After King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, and the officials of Judah had been taken from Jerusalem, along with all the free men, craftsmen, and prisoners in chains from Jerusalem,
by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom King Zedekiah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon, saying:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the exiles who were taken captive from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there, and do not decrease.
Live in peace in the land to which I have taken you captive, and pray to the Lord for its people, because in their peace you too will have peace.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let your false prophets who are among you, or your diviners, deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you dream.
For they prophesy falsely to you in my name, and I did not send them, says the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: When Babylon is close to completing seventy years, I will visit you and fulfill my good words concerning you by bringing you back to this place.
For I know the plans that I make and will make for you, says the Lord, plans for peace and not for harm, to give you hope afterward.
And you will call upon me and go and stand in prayer before me, and I will hear you.
And you will seek me and find me, because you will seek me with all your heart.

“And I will appear to you,” says the Lord, “and restore you from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I scattered you,” says the Lord, “and bring you back to the place from which I took you captive.”
For you say, “The Lord has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.”
For thus says the Lord concerning the king who sits on David’s throne and all the people who live in that city, your brothers who did not go into captivity with you:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Look, I will send famine, sword, and death upon them, and I will make them like rotten figs, [?], which cannot be eaten because of their rottenness.

And I will pursue them with sword, famine, and death, and make them an object of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, a ruin, an object of hissing and reproach among all the nations where I scatter them.
Because they did not listen to my words, says the Lord, although I sent them my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; and you did not listen, says the Lord.
But you, all the captives whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who prophesied falsely to you in my name: Look, I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, and he will kill them before your eyes.
And all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will use their fate as a curse, saying, “May the Lord make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of the Babylonians roasted in the fire.”

For they committed lawless acts in Israel, committed adultery with the wives of their fellow citizens, and spoke false messages in my name, which I did not command them to speak. I myself know and am a witness, says the Lord.
And you shall say to Shemaiah the Elamite:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you sent letters in my name to all the people in Jerusalem, although I did not send you in my name, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, and to all the priests, saying:

“The Lord has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be an overseer in the house of the Lord over everyone who prophesies and everyone who recounts a vision, so that you may put them in confinement, in the [?].
Why, then, have you not punished Jeremiah of Anathoth, who prophesies to you?
For he sent word to us in Babylon, saying, ‘The time is far off. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.’”
And Zephaniah the priest read the letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
Send word to all the captives and say: Thus says the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Elamite: Because Shemaiah prophesied to you, although I did not send him, and made you trust in falsehood,

therefore thus says the Lord: Look, I will punish Shemaiah the Elamite and his descendants. He will have no one living among you to see the good that I will do for you, says the Lord, because he spoke of turning away from the Lord.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Write for yourself in a book all the words that I commanded you.

For look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will bring back the captives of my people Israel and Judah, says the Lord, and return them to the land that I gave their fathers, and they will possess it.
And these are the words that the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
Thus says the Lord: You will hear a cry of terror and the sound of dreadful news, at which waists will tremble, and there will be no deliverance or peace.
Ask and see whether a male has ever given birth. For I saw every man with his hands on his waist like a woman in labor, and all their faces turned pale.
Alas, for that day is great, and there is none like it! It is a time of unbearable distress for Jacob, yet he will be saved from it.
And on that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will break the yoke from their necks and tear apart their bonds, and they will no longer be subject to foreigners.
Instead, they will serve the Lord their God, and I will raise up David as their king.

But do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, says the Lord, and do not be terrified, Israel. For behold, I will save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and rest and prosper, and there will be no one to terrify him.

For I am with you, says the Lord, to save you. I will diminish the nations among which I scatter you, but I will not put an end to you. I will discipline you justly, and I will certainly not acquit you.
Thus says the Lord: I have made your injury severe, and your wounds are painful.
There is no one to plead your case. You were treated for your pains, but it did you no good.
All your friends have forgotten you and do not inquire about you. For I struck you with an enemy's blows, with severe discipline, because of all your injustices; your sins have multiplied.

Why do you cry out over your injury? Yet I will not put an end to you. Your pains are severe because of the multitude of your lawless deeds. Your sins have grown grievous; they have brought this upon you.

Therefore, all who devoured you will be devoured, and all your enemies will eat their own flesh, because of your many injustices, which increased, and your sins, which brought this upon you. Those who destroy you will suffer destruction, and I will give all who plunder you over to plunder.
For I will bring you healing for your painful wounds and heal you, says the Lord. For you were called Scattered, Zion, and this is your prey, for whoever seeks her will not find her.

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will reverse the exile of Jacob's tents and have mercy on his captivity. The city will be built on its height, and the temple will be established according to its proper order.
“Singers and the sound of merrymakers will come forth from them. I will multiply them, and they will not decrease; I will spread them out, and they will not dwindle.”
They will enter as before, and their testimonies will stand firm before my eyes, and I will call their oppressors to account.

And there will be those stronger than them over them, and their ruler will come from among them. I will gather them, and they will return to me. For who is it who has given his heart to return to the Lord? says the Lord.
You will be my people, and I will be your God.
For the Lord's anger has gone forth in fury; stormy wrath has gone forth and will come upon the ungodly.
Let the Lord's fierce anger not turn back until he has done and fulfilled the desire of his heart. In the last days you will understand this.
At that time, says the Lord, I will be the God of the people of Israel, and they will be my people.
Thus says the Lord: They found heat in the wilderness there, together with those who perished by the sword. Go; do not destroy Israel.
The Lord appeared to him openly: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you in compassion.
Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourine and go out among the gatherings of dancers.
Again you will plant vineyards on the mountain of Samaria. You will plant the plants and bless them.
For the day of the herald's call has arrived on the mountains of Ephraim: Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.
Thus says the Lord: Rejoice for Jacob; be glad and shout over the leaders of the nations. Make yourselves heard, give praise, and say, “The Lord has saved his people, the remnant of Israel.”

Look, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth at the Passover festival, and they will bear very many children. Among them will be the blind, the lame, pregnant women, and women who have given birth. Together, a great assembly will return here.

They went out weeping, and I will bring them back with comfort, to rest beside streams of water, along a straight road, and they will not stray on it. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the Lord, you nations, and proclaim it in distant islands. Say, “The one who scattered Israel will gather him and guard him as a herdsman guards his flock.”
For the Lord has redeemed Jacob and rescued him from the hands of those who oppressed him.

They will come and be glad and rejoice on Mount Zion. They will come to the good things of the Lord, to a land of grain, wine, produce, and herds of cattle and sheep. Their souls will be like a tree laden with fruit, and they will hunger no more.
Then the young women will rejoice in gatherings of young men, and the old will be glad. I will turn their mourning into joy and make them glad after their sorrow.
I will delight and intoxicate the souls of the priests, the sons of Levi, and my people will be filled with my good things, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping, and cries of grief. Rachel was weeping for her children and would not be comforted over her children, because they were no more.
Thus says the Lord: Stop your weeping and let your eyes cease shedding tears, for there is a reward for your work, says the Lord, and they will return from the land of their enemies.
There will be hope for your future, says the Lord, and your children will dwell within their own borders.
I have indeed heard Ephraim’s lament: “You disciplined me, Lord, and I was disciplined, but I did not learn, like an untrained calf. Turn me back, and I will return, for you are the Lord my God.”
After my captivity I repented, and after I came to understand, I sighed over the day of my shame. I showed you that I had borne disgrace from my youth.
Is Ephraim my beloved son, a child I delight in? Because my words concern him, I will surely remember him again. Therefore I hastened on his behalf; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.
Approach yourself in person. Bring punishment upon yourself, Zion. Set your heart upon your shoulders; go along the road. Return, virgin Israel; return again to your cities in mourning.
How long will you wander, dishonored daughter? For the Lord has established salvation in a new planting; people will go about in salvation.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: They will again say these words in the land of Judah and in its cities when I bring back its captives: “Blessed is the Lord on his righteous and holy mountain.”
The inhabitants of Judea, with all their cities and their workers, will enjoy abundance with their flocks.
“For I have given every thirsty soul drink and filled every hungry soul.”
Therefore I awoke and looked, and my sleep had been sweet to me.
Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the offspring of humans and the offspring of animals.
Just as I watched over them to uproot, overthrow, tear down, destroy, and afflict, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, says the Lord.
“In those days they will no longer say, ‘The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge.’”
Rather, each will die for his own sins. Every person who eats sour grapes will have his own teeth set on edge.
Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

Not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of the Egyptians, because they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.

But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

They shall no longer each teach their neighbor and each their brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says the Lord. For I will forgive their wrongdoing and no longer remember their sins.
Thus says the Lord, who gave the sun for light by day, the moon and the stars by fixed ordinance for light by night, and a roar in the sea, whose waves roar: The Lord Almighty is his name.
If these ordinances cease before me, says the Lord, then the people of Israel shall also cease to be a nation before my eyes for all time.

Thus says the Lord: If the heavens rise into the heights, and if the foundations of the earth sink into the depths, I will not reject the whole people of Israel, says the Lord, because of all that they have done.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when a city shall be built for the Lord, from the tower of Hanamel to the Corner Gate.
And a [?] and its measure shall extend farther straight ahead to the hill of Gareb, and it shall circle around the choicest stones.

And the whole valley of Phakadim and of the ashes, and all Saremoth, as far as the valley of Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, shall be holy to the Lord. They shall never again be uprooted or demolished.
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah. That year was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Babylonians.
At that time the army of the king of the Babylonians was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was held in custody in the prison courtyard, which was in the palace of the king of Judah.
Where King Zedekiah confined him, saying, “Why do you prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Look, I am giving this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it’?”

And Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, for he shall surely be handed over to the king of the Babylonians. He shall speak with him face to face, and his eyes shall see the king’s eyes.
And Zedekiah shall enter Babylon and remain there until I attend to him, says the Lord. Why do you fight against the Chaldeans, when you will have no success?
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
Look, Hanamel, the son of Shallum your uncle, is coming to you and will say, ‘Buy my field in Anathoth, for by right of kinship it falls to you to acquire it.’

And Hanamel, the son of Shallum my uncle, came to me in the prison courtyard, according to the word of the Lord, and said to me, ‘Buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for it is your duty to acquire the inheritance, and you yourself are the eldest.’ Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
And I bought the field in Anathoth from Hanamel, my uncle’s son, and weighed out silver for him: seven shekels and ten pieces of silver.
And I wrote the deed and sealed it, appointed witnesses, and weighed the silver on the scales.
And I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, according to the command and the legal provisions, and the open copy.

And I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, in the presence of Hanamel, my uncle’s son, and in the presence of those who were there and signed the deed of purchase, before all the Jews who were sitting in the prison courtyard.
And I instructed Baruch in their presence, saying:
Thus says the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel: Take these deeds—the sealed deed of purchase and the unsealed deed—and put them in an earthenware jar so that they may last for many days.
For thus says the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel: Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.
After giving the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I stood in prayer before the LORD and said:
O Lord GOD, you made heaven and earth by your great power and your uplifted arm, and nothing can be hidden from you.
You show mercy to a thousand generations and repay the sins of fathers into the laps of their children after them. You are the great and mighty God; the LORD of hosts is his name.

You are great in counsel and mighty in deeds, the Almighty LORD whose name is great. Your eyes are open to all the ways of humanity, to give each person according to their way and according to the fruit of their conduct.
You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, continuing to this day among Israel and among the inhabitants of the earth, and you made a name for yourself, as it is today.
You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, and with great manifestations.
You gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

They entered and took possession of it, but they did not obey your voice or walk according to your commands. They did not do any of the things you commanded them to do, and they caused all these disasters to come upon themselves.

And now, look, an army has reached this city to capture it, and the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans who wage war against it, because of sword, famine, and death. Just as you said, so it has happened, as you yourself see.
Yet you, LORD, said to me, ‘Buy yourself a field with silver,’ and I wrote a deed, sealed it, and appointed witnesses, even though the city has been handed over to the Chaldeans.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Look, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Can anything be hidden from me?
Therefore thus says the LORD: This city will certainly be handed over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Chaldeans will come to fight against this city and burn it with fire. They will set fire to the houses on whose roofs people burned incense to Baal and offered sacrifices to foreign gods to provoke me.

The children of Israel and the children of Judah have done nothing but evil before my eyes from their youth. Indeed, the children of Israel have angered me with the works of their hands, says the LORD.
“This city has provoked my anger and wrath from the day they built it until today, so that I would wipe it away from my sight.”

Because of all the evil that the children of Israel and the children of Judah committed to provoke me—they themselves, their kings, their leaders, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me, not their faces. I taught them, teaching them early each morning, but they did not listen or accept correction.
They placed their abominations in the house that bears my name.

As part of their abominable conduct, they built altars to Baal in the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom to offer their sons and daughters to Molech. I did not command them to do this, nor did it enter my heart that they should commit this abomination and cause Judah to sin.
And now thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning this city, of which you said, ‘It has been handed over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon through sword, famine, and captivity.’
Look, I will gather them from every land where I scattered them in my anger, my fury, and my great wrath. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in safety.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them a different heart and one way, so that they may fear me all their days, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will not turn back from doing them good, and I will put the fear of me in their hearts so that they do not rebel against me.
I will attend to doing them good, and I will plant them firmly in this land with all my heart and all my soul.
For this is what the Lord says: Just as I brought all these great calamities upon this people, so I will bring upon them the good things I spoke of concerning them.
Fields will again be bought in this land, of which you said, “It is deserted, without people or animals, and has been handed over to the Chaldeans.”

Fields will be bought with silver, deeds will be written and sealed, and witnesses will be appointed in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, in the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the Shephelah, and in the towns of the Negev. For I will bring back their captives, says the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the prison courtyard, saying:
This is what the Lord says, who made this land and formed it to establish it—the Lord is his name:
Call to me, and I will answer you and tell you great and mighty things that you do not know.
For this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah, torn down for siege mounds and ramparts,

of those who have come to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of people whom I struck down in my anger and fury. I turned my face away from them because of all their wickedness.
Look, I will bring [?] for healing, and I will heal them and reveal to them the sound of peace and faithfulness.
I will bring back the captives of Judah and the captives of Jerusalem, and I will rebuild them as they were before.
I will cleanse them of all the wrongs they committed against me, and I will no longer remember the sins they committed against me when they rebelled against me.

It will be a joy, a praise, and an honor to me before all the peoples of the earth who hear of all the good I will do for them. They will fear and be distressed at all the goodness and all the peace I will provide for them.

Thus says the Lord: “In this place, of which you say, ‘It is desolate, without people or animals,’ in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, in the desolate places where there are no people, no inhabitants, and no animals, there will again be heard

The sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, who will say, “Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.” They will bring sacrifices of praise into the house of the Lord, for I will bring back the captives of this land as before, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord of hosts says: In this ruined place, where there are no people or animals, and in all its towns, there will again be dwellings for shepherds and resting places for flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the Shephelah, in the towns of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says the Lord.
Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will fulfill the good words I spoke concerning the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time, I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David, who will carry out justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell in safety. And this is the name by which she will be called: “The Lord is our righteousness.”
For thus says the Lord: “David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the Levitical priests will never lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, sacrifice sacrifices, and burn incense every day.”
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
“Thus says the Lord: If you break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night do not come at their appointed times,
then my covenant with David my servant will also be broken, so that he has no son to reign on his throne, and likewise my covenant with the Levitical priests, my ministers.
Just as the hosts of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.”
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

“Do you not see what these people are saying? They say, ‘The Lord has rejected the two families that he chose.’ And they provoke my people to anger, so that they are no longer a nation in their sight.
Thus says the Lord: If I have not firmly established my covenant of day and night and of heaven and earth,

then I will also reject the descendants of Jacob and of David my servant, so as not to take from his descendants a ruler over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.”

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up, and his entire army, all the land under his authority, and all the nations were fighting against Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah. He said:

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: “Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it and burn it with fire.’”
“And you will not escape from his hands, but you will certainly be captured and handed over to him. Your eyes will see his eyes, and you will speak with him face to face, and you will go to Babylon.
Now hear the words of the Lord, Zedekiah, king of Judah. Thus says the Lord concerning you: You will not die by the sword.”

“But you will die in peace. Just as they mourned your fathers, the former kings who came before you, so they will mourn you, saying, ‘Alas, alas, lord!’ And they will lament you, for I have spoken great things,” says the Lord.
And Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah, king of Judah, in Jerusalem.

And the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the remaining cities of Judah, against Lachish and Azekah, for these were the fortified cities that remained among the cities of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim freedom to them,
that each person should set free his male slave and his female slave, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, and that no man of the people of Judah should enslave his brother.

And all the leaders and all the people who had entered the covenant to set free their male slaves and their female slaves, the Hebrew men and the Hebrew women, and no longer enslave them, turned; they listened and released them.
But afterward they turned back and brought back the male slaves and female slaves whom they had set free, and held them as male slaves and female slaves.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
“Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day when I delivered them from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and I said:

‘When six years are completed, you must release your Hebrew brother who has been sold to you and has served you for six years. You must set him free from your service.’ But your fathers did not listen to me or incline their ears.
And today they turned to do what is pleasing in my sight, each proclaiming freedom to his neighbor, and they made the covenant before me in the house that bears my name.

But you turned back and profaned my name, each of you taking back his male slave and his female slave, whom you had set free of your own will, and you brought them back to be your male and female slaves.

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: You did not listen to me and proclaim freedom, each of you for his brother and each of you for his neighbor. Look, I will proclaim freedom for you, says the Lord—to the sword, to famine, and to death—and I will scatter you throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.
I will hand over the men who violated my covenant and did not keep the terms of my covenant that they made before me, like the calf that they cut apart and passed between its pieces:
the officials of Judah, the officials of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf.
I will hand them over to their enemies and to those who seek their lives, and I will cast out their corpses as food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth.
And I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials to their enemies, to those who seek their lives, and to the army of the king of Babylon, which has come against them.

Look, I will give the command, says the Lord, and bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it with fire. And I will make the cities of Judah a wilderness, without inhabitants.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
Go to the house of the Rechabites and summon them. Bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of its chambers, and give them wine to drink.
And I brought Jeconiah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, his brothers, all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.

I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the son of Hanan son of Gedaliah, the man of God. It was beside the room of the officials, above the quarters of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the doorkeeper.
And I placed before the sons of the Rechabites a vessel full of wine and cups, and I said to them, “Drink this wine.”
And they said, “We will not drink wine, because Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘Neither you nor your children shall ever drink wine.
You shall not build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards. Instead, you shall live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days in the land where you wander.’
And we obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, in everything he commanded us: not to drink wine all our days, neither we nor our wives nor our sons nor our daughters;
and not to build houses or live in them. We have had no vineyards, fields, or crops.
We have lived in tents, and we have obeyed and done everything that Jonadab our father commanded us.
But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up into this land, we said, ‘Let us go up and enter Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Assyrians, and let us live there.’”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, “Will you not accept instruction and listen to my words?” says the Lord.

The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command he gave his sons not to drink wine, and they have not drunk it to this day, because they obeyed their father’s command. But I spoke to you beforehand, and you did not listen to me.

And I sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them early [?]: “Turn, each of you, from your evil way, and improve your deeds. Do not follow foreign gods to serve them, and you will dwell in the land that I gave you and your ancestors.” But you did not incline your ears or listen to me.
The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab upheld the command of their father, which he had given them, but this people did not listen to me.

Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: “Look, I will bring upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disasters that I pronounced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen; I called them and they did not answer me.”

And Jeremiah said to the house of Rechab: “Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab listened to their father’s command and kept all his instructions, doing everything that their father commanded them—”
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: “The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me all the days of the earth.”
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Take a scroll for yourself and write on it all the words that I commanded you concerning Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the day when I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah king of Judah, until today.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear of all the disasters that I intend to bring upon them, so that each of them may turn from his evil way, and I may forgive their lawlessness and their sins.”
Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on the scroll, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the Lord that he had commanded him.
Jeremiah instructed Baruch, saying: “I am imprisoned and cannot enter the house of the Lord.

But you shall enter and read from the scroll that you wrote at my dictation the words of the Lord in the hearing of the people in the house of the Lord on the day of fasting. You shall also read them in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come from their towns.
Perhaps compassion will enter their hearts before the Lord, and each of them will turn from his evil ways, for great are the wrath and anger that the Lord has pronounced against this people.”
Baruch son of Neriah did everything that Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, reading from the scroll the messages of the Lord in the house of the Lord.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people of Jerusalem, all the people who came from the towns of Judah to Jerusalem, and the house of Judah gathered for a fast before the Lord.

Baruch read Jeremiah’s words from the scroll in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan, the chief scribe, at the entrance of the new gate of the house of the Lord, in the hearing of all the people.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the messages of the Lord from the scroll,

he went down to the king’s house, to the chief scribe’s office. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the chief scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

All the officials sent Jehudi son of Nathan, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in your hands the scroll that you read in the hearing of the people, and come here.” Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hands and went down to them.
They said to him, “Please read it again in our hearing.” And Baruch read it in their hearing.
When they heard all the messages, they conferred, each with his neighbor, and said to Baruch, “We will certainly report all these words to the king.”
They questioned Baruch, saying, “Please tell us where you got all these words that you wrote. From whose mouth did they come?”
And Baruch said to them, “Jeremiah himself recited all these words to me, and I wrote them in the scroll with ink.”
The officials said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.”
They went in to the king in the hall, leaving the scroll for safekeeping in the house of Elishama the chief scribe, and reported all the words to the king.
The king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll. He took it from the house of Elishama the chief scribe, and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and all the officials standing around the king.
The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a burning brazier before him.

Whenever Jehudi had read three or four pages, the king cut them off with the chief scribe’s knife and threw them into the fire in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed in the brazier’s fire.
Neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all those words made any inquiry or tore their robes.
Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
And the king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdiel to seize Baruch the chief scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but they went into hiding.
After the king had burned the scroll and all the words that Baruch had written from Jeremiah’s mouth, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
“Take another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, ‘Thus says the Lord: You burned that scroll and said, “Why did you write on it and say that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land, removing both people and animals from it?”
Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one left to sit on David’s throne, and his dead body will lie cast out in the heat by day and in the cold by night.

I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants according to his lawlessness. I will bring upon them, upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the land of Judah all the calamities that I spoke against them, but they did not listen.’”

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the chief scribe. He wrote in it, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire, and still more words were added to it, beyond those.
Zedekiah son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made king over Judah, reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim.
Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord that he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehoahaz son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Pray for us to the Lord our God.”

And Jeremiah passed through the crowd and came and went, and they did not put him in prison. And Pharaoh’s army came out of the land of the Egyptians. When the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
“Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Say this to the king of Judah who sent you to me to seek me: The army of Pharaoh that came out to help you will return to Egypt.
The Chaldeans will return here and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it with fire.
Thus says the Lord: Do not think to yourselves, ‘The Chaldeans have gone away from us.’ They will not withdraw from you.”
Even if you slaughter the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, the wounded men who remain among them will rise, each from his place, and burn this city with fire.
And when the army of the Chaldeans withdrew from Jerusalem before Pharaoh’s army,
Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to buy a share of property there among the people.

He reached the Benjamin Gate, and there was a man there who had been put in charge, named Saru, son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. He seized Jeremiah the prophet and said, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
Jeremiah said, “You are lying! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But he did not listen to him, and Saru seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were angry with Jeremiah, beat him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the chief scribe, for they had made his house into a prison.
Jeremiah came into the dungeon, into [?], and Jeremiah remained there for many days.

King Zedekiah sent for him and summoned him, and the king questioned him secretly in his house, saying to him, “Is there any message from the Lord?” And Jeremiah said, “Yes, there is.” And he said, “You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”
Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What sin have I committed against you, your servants, or the people, that you put me in prison?
And where are your prophets who prophesied and said, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you in this land’?
Now listen, I beg you, my lord the king. Let my plea for mercy come before you. Why do you send me back to the house of Jonathan the chief scribe, where I will die?”

King Zedekiah gave orders, and they put him in the prison and gave him a loaf of bread each day from the bakers outside, until all the bread in the city was gone. And Jeremiah remained in the prison courtyard.
And Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehoahaz son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying:
Thus says the Lord: “Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live. He will gain his life as his spoil, and he will live.
For thus says the Lord: ‘This city will certainly be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.’”

The officials said to the king, “Let that man be killed, because he weakens the hands of the fighting men remaining in this city and the hands of all the people by speaking these words to them. For that man does not speak words of benefit and peace to the people, but of harm.”
King Zedekiah said, “Look, he is in your hands,” for he had no power against them in anything.

They took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king’s son, which was in the prison courtyard. They lowered Jeremiah into the cistern with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah remained in the mud.
Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch who was in the king’s palace, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-melech went out from the king’s palace to him, spoke to the king, and said,

“My lord the king, those men have acted wickedly in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, for they have thrown him into the cistern, and he is dying inside. You have done wrong by killing the man of God through this famine, for no bread can be found in this city.”
The king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, “Take thirty men from here with you, and bring the prophet up out of the cistern so that he does not die.”
Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the king’s palace, to the underground treasury chamber. He took old rugs and old ropes from there and dropped them down to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, “Put these old rugs and pieces of wool under your armpits, beneath the ropes.” And Jeremiah did so.
They pulled him up with the ropes and brought him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the prison courtyard.

King Zedekiah sent for the prophet and summoned him to the house of Assaghisai, which was in the house of the Lord. The king said to him, “I am going to ask you something. Do not hide the matter from me.”
Jeremiah said to the king, “If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
King Zedekiah secretly swore to him, saying, “As the Lord lives, who gave us this breath of life, I will not kill you or hand you over to the men who seek your life.”

Jeremiah said to him, “This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned with fire. You and your household will live.
But if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire. You will not escape from their hands.”
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “There are some matters between me and the Jews who have fled to the Chaldeans. They might hand me over to them, and they might abuse me.”
Jeremiah said, “They will not hand you over. Only listen to the words of the Lord that I speak to you, and it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
But if you are unwilling to go out, this is what the Lord has shown me:

Look, all the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they will say, ‘The men who were at peace with you have deceived you and overcome you. They will cause your feet to stumble and turn away from you.’

They will bring out all your wives and your children to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape from his hands, for you will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire.”
The king said to him, “Man, let no one know anything of these words, lest you die.
If the officials hear that I have spoken with you and come to you and say, ‘Tell us what you said to the king. Do not hide it from us, and we will not kill you,’ or, ‘What did the king say to you?’
you shall say to them, ‘I pleaded with the king not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.’”
All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He told them everything the king had instructed him to say, and they left him alone, because the matter had not become known.
Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the prison until the time when Jerusalem was captured.

When Jerusalem was captured, it happened that in the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his entire army to Jerusalem, and they besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city wall was breached,

and all the commanders of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Sarmagada, Nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the fighting men saw them, they fled and left the city by night along the road through the royal garden, through the gate between the walls. They went out along the road to the Arabah.

The Chaldean army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and brought him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
The king of Babylon killed Zedekiah’s sons at Riblah before his eyes. The king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
And he blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the king’s house and the houses of the people with fire, and tore down the wall of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, deported to Babylon the rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had deserted to him, and the destitute people who remained.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left behind in the land of Judah some of the poor people who had nothing, and gave them vineyards and irrigated fields that day.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, entrusted Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, with these instructions:
“Take him and look after him. Do him no harm, but do for him whatever he asks you.”
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, Nebushazban, the chief eunuch, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the officials of the king of Babylon sent
and took Jeremiah out of the prison. They handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and brought him to the house. He remained there among the people.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was in confinement in the prison courtyard, saying:

“Go and tell Ebed-melech the Ethiopian: This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing my word upon this city for harm and not for good, and it will happen before your eyes on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, says the Lord, and I will not hand you over to the men you fear.
For I will surely save you, and you will not fall by the sword. Your life will be your prize, because you trusted in me, says the Lord.”

The word that came concerning Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released him at Ramah. For they had taken him, bound with shackles, from among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being deported to Babylon.
The captain of the guard took him and said to him, “The Lord your God declared these calamities against this place.”
“The Lord brought this about and did as he had said, because you sinned against the Lord and did not obey his voice. So this has happened to you.

And now, look, today I am releasing you from the shackles on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if it seems bad to you to come with me to Babylon, remain here. Look, the whole land is before you; go wherever it seems good and pleasing to you to go.

While I am still here, go to whomever you wish, and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed over the land of Judah, and live with him among the people. Otherwise, go wherever you please.” The captain of the guard gave him provisions and gifts and released him.
Jeremiah came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived there among the people who remained in the land.

All the army commanders who were out in the countryside, together with their troops, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had entrusted to him men, women, many people, and some of the poor people of the land whom he had not deported to Babylon.

They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai son of Netophath, and Jezaniah son of Maacah, together with the men who were with them.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and to the men who were with them, saying, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and pay tribute to the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.
As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to meet the Chaldeans who come to us. But you are to gather wine and fruit, collect oil in your vessels, and live in your towns, which you took by your valor.”

And all the Jews who were in the land of Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judea and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as their overseer.
