All the Jews returned from all the places to which they had been scattered. They came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered a very great quantity of wine and fruit.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were out in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
And they said to him, “Do you know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent to Ishmael son of Nethaniah to have you killed?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

And Johanan son of Kareah said secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, “Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and let no one know. Otherwise he may kill you, and the Jews who have gathered around you will be scattered, and the remnant of Judah will perish.”
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do what you have said, for you have spoken falsely about Ishmael.”

And in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal family, and the king’s servants, and ten men with him came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at Mizpah.

And Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword and killed him, whom the king of the Babylonians had appointed over the land.
And Ishmael slaughtered all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and all the Chaldeans found there, the fighting men.
And on the second day after Gedaliah had been killed there, when no one knew about it,
men came from Shechem, Salem, and Samaria—eighty men with their beards shaved and their clothes torn, mourning, with manna and frankincense in their hands to bring to the house of the Lord.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he came near them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
And when they entered the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them in the middle of the city and threw them into a cistern, he and the men who were with him.

But ten men were found there who said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us, for we have stores in the field: wheat, barley, honey, and oil.” So he spared them and did not kill them along with their fellow men.

And the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men he had slaughtered because of Gedaliah was a large cistern that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael led away all the people who remained at Mizpah, including the king’s daughters, together with all the poor people who were at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. And Ishmael son of Nethaniah rose early in the morning and went across to the Ammonites.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
They gathered all their soldiers and set out to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him beside the great waters at Gibeon.
And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, they rejoiced.
And all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned back to them and came to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.

And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him took all the remaining people whom he had rescued from Ishmael son of Nethaniah at Mizpah after he had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam: the mighty fighting men, the women, the men, and the eunuchs whom he brought from the land of the Gibeonites.
And they went and stayed in the land of Geruth Chimham, opposite Bethlehem, intending to go into the land of the Egyptians.
Away from the Chaldeans, for they were struck with fear of them, because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And all the commanders of the forces, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, approached.

And they said to Jeremiah the prophet, “Let our plea for mercy be accepted before you, and pray for us to the Lord your God, for this remnant, because we are left as a few out of many, as your own eyes see us.
Let the Lord your God tell us the way we should go and what we should do.”

And Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard you. Look, I will pray to the Lord your God as you have asked. Whatever answer the Lord gives, I will tell you, and I will not hide a single word from you.”
And they said to Jeremiah, “May the Lord be a just and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word with which the Lord your God sends you to us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us; and we will obey the voice of the Lord our God.”
And after ten days, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
And he called Jonah son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
And he said to them, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says, to whom you sent me to plead for mercy before him:
‘If you remain in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, because I have relented concerning the harm I said I would do to you.
Do not fear the king of the Babylonians, whose presence terrified you. Do not fear him, says the Lord, because I am with you to save you and deliver you from their hands.
And I will grant [?] compassion, and I will have mercy on you and bring you back to your land.
But if you say, “We will not remain in this land, and we will not obey the voice of the Lord our God,
but we will go to the land of the Egyptians, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or hunger for bread, and we will live there,”
then hear the message of the Lord, you remnant of Judea. This is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you firmly set your faces toward entering Egypt and living there,
then the sword you feared will find you there in the land of the Egyptians, and the famine you dreaded will overtake you there in the land of the Egyptians, and there you will die.
And all the men who set their faces toward entering the land of the Egyptians to live there will perish by sword, famine, and death. None of them will escape the harm that I will bring upon them.

For this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Just as my furious anger poured down upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will pour down upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become a wasteland and exiles, a curse and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again.’
Concerning this, the Lord spoke about you and the remnant of Judah, saying, ‘Do not enter Egypt.’ But now know for certain that I bear witness against you today.

For you have done harm to yourselves, because you sent me to the Lord your God and said, ‘Pray for us to the Lord our God, and tell us everything that the Lord our God says to you, and we will do it.’
And I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, with whose message he sent me to you.
And now know that you will perish by sword, famine, and death in the place where you wish to go and live.”
And when Jeremiah finished speaking to all the people all the words of the Lord their God, with which the Lord their God had sent him to them,

And Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, “You are speaking lies. The LORD our God did not send you to us to say, ‘Do not enter Egypt to live there.’
“Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is stirring you up against us, so that you will hand us over to the Chaldeans to slaughter us and carry us away as captives to Babylon.”
And Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders, and all the people did not obey the voice of the LORD and remain in the land of Judah.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered, to live in the land of Judah—

the men, women, children, the king’s daughters, and the people whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
And they went to the land of Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they came to Tahpanhes.
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying:
“Take large stones and bury them secretly in the brickwork at the entrance to Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

“And say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I will send for and bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. He will set his throne upon these stones that I have hidden, and he will take his weapon with him upon them.
“‘And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death, to death; those destined for captivity, to captivity; and those destined for the sword, to the sword.

And he will set fire to the houses of their gods and burn them and carry them away captive. He will search the land of Egypt as a shepherd searches his clothing, and he will depart from there in peace.
“‘And he will shatter the pillars of the City of the Sun, which is in the land of Egypt, and burn the temples of their gods with fire.’”
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who lived in the land of Egypt, who dwelt in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros, saying:
Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: “You yourselves know all the disasters that I brought upon Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah. Look, today they stand in ruins, without inhabitants,
“because of the evil they committed to provoke me, for they went to burn incense and worship foreign gods whom neither you nor your ancestors knew.
“And I sent all my servants the prophets to you, morning after morning, saying, ‘Do not do this abominable thing that I hate.’
“And they did not listen to me or incline their ears to turn from their evil and stop burning incense to foreign gods.
“And my wrathful anger poured out and blazed at the gates of Judah and outside Jerusalem, and they became ruins and a wilderness, as they are today.
“And now, thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing such great evil to yourselves, cutting off from Judah your men, women, and nursing infants, so that none of you remain,

“provoking me with the works of your hands, burning incense to foreign gods in the land of Egypt, where you have entered to live, so that you will be destroyed and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth,

“so that you do not forget the evil deeds of your ancestors, the evil deeds of the kings of Judah, the evil deeds of their wives, your own evil deeds, and the evil deeds of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and outside Jerusalem.
“And they have not stopped to this day, nor have they feared or followed my laws and the commands that I set before you and before your ancestors.
“Therefore, thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am setting my face against you for disaster, to destroy all Judah.”

And they will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to enter the land of Egypt and live here, to destroy all the remnant who are in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and perish by famine. From the least to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine, and they will become an object of cursing, destruction, malediction, and reproach.
And I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine, and death.

And none of the remnant of Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt will survive to return to the land of Judah, where they longed in their hearts to return and live. They will not return, except for those who escape.

Then all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to foreign gods, and all the women who stood there in great assemblies, and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
We will not listen to the word you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord.

Instead, we will certainly do everything that comes from our mouths: burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and present offerings to her, as we, our fathers, our kings, and our rulers did in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of bread, lived in comfort, and saw no trouble.
But when we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and presenting offerings to her, we lacked everything and perished by sword and famine.
And when we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and presented offerings to her, was it without our husbands that we made cakes and pastries for her and presented offerings to her?
Jeremiah answered all the mighty men among the people, together with the women, and all the people who had given him that answer, and said:

Did not the Lord remember the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem—you, your fathers, your kings, your rulers, and the people of the land—and did it not come into his heart?
The Lord could no longer endure your evil deeds and the abominations you committed. So your land became a ruin, a wilderness, and an object of cursing, without inhabitants, as it is today.

Because of those to whom you burn incense, and through whom you sin against the Lord, and because you do not listen to the Lord’s voice or walk according to his laws, his testimonies, and his commands, these troubles have overtaken you, as they have today.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and all the women: Hear the words of the Lord, all you people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths; fulfill it with your hands. You say, ‘We will certainly fulfill the vow we made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and present offerings.’ Stand firmly by your vow, then, and carry out your pledge.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt. Behold, I have sworn by my great self, says the Lord God, that my name will no longer be spoken by the mouth of any man of Judah, saying, ‘As the Lord lives,’ anywhere in the land of Egypt.
For behold, I am keeping watch over them to afflict them, not to do them good. All the men of Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they dwindle away.

Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. And all the remnant of Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt will know whose word stands, mine or theirs.
And this will be a sign to you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words against you for harm will surely stand.

Thus says the Lord: Look, I will give Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, into the hands of his enemy and into the hands of those seeking his life, just as I gave King Zedekiah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a book from Jeremiah’s dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
You said, “Woe to me! Woe to me! For the Lord has added hardship to my pains. I lay down with groaning and found no rest.”
You shall say this to him: Thus says the Lord: Look, what I built, I myself will tear down, and what I planted, I myself will uproot—all that land.
And do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for look, I will bring disaster upon all flesh, says the Lord. But I will give you your life as a prize wherever you go.
Concerning Egypt. The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning all the nations.

Concerning Egypt, concerning the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Take up weapons and shields; advance into battle.
Harness the horses; mount, fully armed men. Put on helmets, bring forward the spears, and put on your armor.

But what is this? Look, they are terrified and moving backward, for their mighty men have been struck down. They have taken flight, and those among them who are surrounded on every side will not turn back, says the Lord.
Let the swift not flee, and let the mighty not escape. In the north, beside the Euphrates River, they grew weak and fell.
Who is this who rises like a river, like rivers with waters piled upon waters?
The waters of Egypt rise like a river, and its waters churn like a river. It says, “I will rise and cover the land; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.”
Mount the horses; prepare the chariots. Go out, warriors of Ethiopia and Libya, armed with weapons; and you Lydians, go out and draw your bows.

For that day belongs to the Lord our God, a day of vengeance, to take vengeance on his enemies. The sword will devour and be satisfied and become drunk with their blood, for the Lord of hosts has a sacrifice in the northern land, beside the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get medicinal resin for the virgin daughter of Egypt. You have multiplied your remedies in vain, and there is no benefit for you from anywhere.
The nations heard the news of your calamity, and the earth was filled with your cry, for warrior stumbled against warrior, and both fell together.
The word that the Lord spoke through Jeremiah the prophet when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to strike the land of Egypt.
Proclaim the news in Egypt, sound it out in Migdol, give instructions in Memphis, and announce in Tahpanhes: Stand up and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured your branches.
Your chosen bull turned and fled. It did not stand, because the Lord weakened it.
The multitude grew weak, and each fell beside his companion. They say, “Come, let us return, each to our own people and each to our own land, away from the Greek sword.”
Call Pharaoh, king of Egypt, by the name Saon and Ebir and Moed.
As I live, says the Lord, whose name is King of hosts, he will come like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
Prepare baggage for captivity for yourself, resident daughter of Egypt, for Memphis will be ruined and will be called “Woe,” because it has no inhabitants.
Egypt is a beautiful, adorned heifer; a severed piece came upon her from the north.
And her mercenaries within her are like fattened oxen, for they too all turned and fled and did not stand firm, because the day of destruction came upon them, and the time of vengeance.
Her voice is like that of a hissing snake, for they will march through the sand. Men bearing axes will come against her like woodcutters.
“Cut down her forest,” says the Lord God, “whose extent no one can measure, for they are more numerous than locusts and cannot be counted.”
The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame; she has been handed over to the northern armies.
The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I will exact vengeance on Amon, her son, on Pharaoh, on the Egyptians, on their gods, on her kings, on Pharaoh and on those who trust in him.
I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to his servants. Afterward she will be inhabited as before,” says the Lord.

“But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear, and do not be terrified, Israel. Look, I will rescue you from far away and your descendants from their captivity. Jacob will return, be at rest and sleep, and no one will torment him.

And you, my servant Jacob, do not fear,” says the Lord, “for I am with you. Though I make an end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you justly, but I will by no means leave you unpunished.”
Concerning the Philistines. The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Thus says the Lord: “Look, waters are rising from the north and will become an overflowing torrent. They will flood the land and everything in it, the city and its inhabitants. People will raise a cry, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail.
At the sound of his charge, of his hooves, of the rumbling of his chariots and the rattling of his wheels, fathers will not turn back to their children, because their hands have gone limp,

on the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines. I will destroy Tyre and Sidon and all their remaining helpers. The Lord will destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the islands and of the Cimmerians.
Baldness will come upon Gaza. Ashkelon and the remnant of the Anakim have been overthrown.
How long will you slaughter, sword of the Lord? How long will you refuse to rest? Return to your sheath; rest and cease!
How can it rest? For the Lord has commanded it to rise against Ashkelon and those remaining along the seacoast.

Concerning Moab. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: “Woe to Nebo, for it has perished! Kiriathaim has been put to shame and captured. Masodab has been put to shame and handed over to defeat.

Moab will no longer have anything to boast of. In Heshbon they plotted evil against her: ‘Come, let us strike her down so that she is no longer a nation.’ It will fall utterly silent; fire will pursue you.
For there is news from Horonaim: destruction and great devastation.
Moab has been shattered. Announce the news in Zoar, for Aloth is filled with weeping.
It will go up weeping along the road to Horonaim. I have heard distress and news of destruction.
Flee and save your lives, and become like a wild donkey in the wilderness.
Because you trusted in your strongholds, troubles will come, and you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into captivity, together with his priests and his rulers.
Destruction will come upon every city, and not one city will escape. The inhabitants will perish, and those of the plain will be destroyed. Thus says the Lord.
Give Moab a sign, for it will be utterly scorched, and all its cities will become a wilderness, with no inhabitants.
Cursed be the one who does the Lord’s work carelessly, and cursed be the one who keeps his sword from its blood.

Moab has been at ease from his youth and has trusted in his glory. He has not been poured from vessel to vessel and has not gone into captivity. Therefore his flavor has remained unchanged, and his aroma has not diminished.
Therefore, look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will send him men to tip him over, and they will tip him over, break his vessels into pieces and shatter his containers.
Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which they trusted.”
How can you say, “We are mighty men and strong warriors”?
Moab and his city have perished, and his choicest young men have fallen in the slaughter, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
The day of Moab is near at hand, and his calamities are approaching very quickly.
Shake him, all of you around him who know his name. Say, “How the beautiful staff, the glorious rod, has been broken!”
Come down from glory and sit in the damp, you who dwell there, daughter of Dibon, for Moab has perished; the destroyer of your strongholds has arrived.
Stand at the crossings of the roads and look, you who dwell in Aroer. Question the fugitives and the survivors, and say, “What has happened?”
Moab has been put to shame, for it has been shattered. Cry out and shout, and proclaim at the Arnon that Moab has perished.
Judgments are coming upon the land of Mishor, upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
and upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
and upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
and upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab has been broken, and his arrogance has been shattered, says the Lord.
Make him drunk, because he spoke arrogantly against the Lord. Moab will strike hand against hand, and he too will become an object of ridicule.
For was not Israel an object of ridicule to you? And was he found among thieves? When you fought against him, you will be taken captive by him.
The inhabitants of Moab left the cities and dwelt in rocky clefts. They became like doves nesting in rocky clefts at the mouths of caves.
We have heard of Moab’s pride, for he has become exceedingly proud—his loftiness, his pride, and his arrogance—and his heart has become exalted.
And I knew his deeds. Surely his arms would be equal to his strength, but he did not act that way.
Therefore raise a cry over Moab; proclaim the news throughout all the regions of Moab, over the men who have been torn, plucked, and blackened, and he will moan.
With the weeping of Jazer, let us weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches stretched across the sea; the cities of Jazer reached them. Destruction has come upon your fruit and upon your harvest.

Joy and gladness have vanished from Carmel and from the land of the Moabites. Wine was in your presses; in the mornings they did not tread, and in the evenings they did not raise the cry of the winepress workers.

At the cry from Heshbon to Elealeh and as far as Jahzah, their cities raised their voices, from Zoar to Horonaim, with tidings in Shalishah; for even the water of Nimrim will be exposed to scorching heat.
And I will destroy Moab, says the Lord, who went up to the altars and offered incense to foreign gods.

Therefore my heart will sound like a pipe over Moab, and my heart over the men shorn beside the walls will be like the sound of a pipe. Therefore whatever he acquired has vanished from among humankind.
Every head everywhere will be shaved, and every beard will be cut off. All hands will beat in mourning, and everyone will be dressed in sackcloth.
On all the rooftops of Moab and in his squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have broken Moab like a vessel useful for nothing, says the Lord.
How he has changed! Raise a lament! How he has turned his back in shame and become an object of ridicule and hostility to everyone around him!
For thus says the Lord: Look, he will swoop like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth has been taken, and his strongholds have been seized. On that day the hearts of Moab’s warriors will be like the hearts of women in labor.
And Moab will perish from among the multitude, because he spoke boastfully against the Lord.
A pit, terror, and a snare are upon you, you who live in Moab.

Whoever flees from terror will fall into the pit, and whoever comes out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring all these things upon Moab in the year when I call it to account, says the Lord.
Those who fled from the snare reached the houses of Heshbon, for fire came out of Heshbon and a flame from the city of Sihon. It devoured the princes of Moab and searched out the sons of Ammon.
Woe to you, Moab! You have destroyed the people of Chemosh, for his sons and his daughters have been taken into captivity.
But I will bring back the captives of Moab in the last days, says the Lord. Thus far are the judgments against Moab.
Concerning the sons of Ammon, thus says the Lord: Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heir? Why has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and why do his people live in their cities?

Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make news of the cities’ disaster heard in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon. It will become a wilderness and a place of destruction, and its altars will be burned with fire. Israel will regain its dominion, says the Lord.

Lament, Heshbon, for Ai has perished! Raise a cry, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, be frantic, mourn, and run back and forth along the fences, for Milcom will go into captivity, together with his priests and princes.
Why do you rejoice in your tents, [?], and in your fields, insolent daughter, who trusted in your treasures and said, ‘Who will come against me?’

Behold, I will bring fear upon you, says the Lord of hosts, from all those who live around you on every side. You will be scattered, each in a different direction, and there will be no one to gather the wanderers.
After that I will bring back the captives of the sons of Ammon, says the Lord.
Concerning Edom, thus says the Lord of hosts: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished among the discerning? Has its wisdom departed?
His place was deceived. Settle deeply, inhabitants of Dedan, for I have brought hardships [?] upon him, at the time when I punish him.
For grape gatherers have come against you, and they will leave you no remnant. Like thieves in the night, they will lay their hands on them.
For I have overthrown Esau and revealed his hidden places, and he will not be able to hide. His offspring have perished at the hands of his brother and his neighbor.
And your orphan cannot remain alive [?], and their widows have put their trust in me.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, those who were not required to drink the cup have indeed drunk it. Will you be completely acquitted? You will not be acquitted, but you will certainly drink.
For I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that you will become a place of ruin, disgrace, wilderness, and curses in the midst of his allotted territory, and all its cities will be ruins forever.
I heard news from the Lord, and he sent a messenger among the nations: Gather together and come against it! Rise up and go to war!
For behold, in a little while I will make you small among the nations, despised among people.

Your disgrace has brought this upon you. The insolence of your heart has made you dwell in the clefts of the rocks and has taken hold of the strength of your lofty hill. Even if you raise your nest like an eagle’s, I will bring you down from there, says the Lord.
Edom will become a wilderness, and everyone who passes through it will be astonished and hiss at all its afflictions.
As Sodom and Gomorrah and their inhabitants were overthrown, says the Lord, so no one will settle there, and no human being will live there.

Behold, like a lion he will come up from the midst of the Jordan to the place of Etham, for I will quickly drive them away from it. Who is chosen there? I will attend to him. Who will oppose me? Who is the shepherd who will stand before me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s plan, which he has devised against the Edomites, and his purpose, which he has devised against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock will strike them; surely their ruins will remain forever.
At the sound of his downfall, the earth shook. News of your disaster reached the Red Sea, and your cry was heard.
Look, he will rise and swoop like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom’s mighty warriors will be like the hearts of women in labor.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad were put to shame because they heard bad news. They were bewildered; they were troubled in the sea and cannot find rest.
Damascus grew weak, turned to flee, and fell. Trembling seized it, and labor pains rushed upon it like a woman giving birth.
And why did he not abandon my city, the town I loved?
Therefore young men will fall in your public squares, and all the fighting men will fall on that day, says the Lord of hosts.
I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the public squares of the sons of Hadad.
Concerning Kedar, concerning the queen of the settlement, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus says the Lord: Rise, go up against Kedar, and strike the sons of Kedem.

They will take their tents and their flocks. They will take for themselves their clothing, all their furnishings and possessions, and their herds of camels. Cry out against them: Destruction on every side!
Flee swiftly! Go deep into hiding, inhabitants of that settlement, says the Lord, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devised a plan against you; he has devised a plan against you.
Rise, go up against the nation that is at rest, that lives at ease, says the Lord. They have neither gates nor bars and live alone.

Their herds of camels will become plunder, and their many flocks will be lost. I will scatter to every wind those whose hair is clipped around their faces, and from every side I will bring destruction upon them, says the Lord.
The settlement will become a dwelling for ostriches and a wilderness forever. No one will live in it, and no human being will dwell there.
Concerning Elam. The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, the bow of Elam has been shattered, the source of their mighty power.
I will bring four winds against Elam from the four quarters of heaven, and I will scatter them to all those winds. There will be no nation to which the wanderers of Elam do not come.

I will terrify them before their enemies who sought their lives, and I will bring upon them [?] according to my furious anger, says the Lord. I will send my sword after them until it has destroyed them completely.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy its kings and nobles, says the Lord.
In the last days I will restore the captives of Elam, says the Lord. At the beginning of King Zedekiah’s reign, this word came concerning Elam.
Concerning the Babylonians. The word that the Lord spoke concerning Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans through Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare it among the nations and make it known. Raise a banner; make it heard; do not conceal it. Say: Babylon has been captured! Bel has been put to shame! The pampered, fearless Merodach has been handed over! Its idols have been put to shame; its abominations have been disgraced.
For a nation has come up against it from the north. It will lay its land waste, and no one will dwell in it. Humans and animals alike have moved away and gone.
In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will travel and come weeping, seeking the Lord their God.
They will ask about the way to Zion, turn in this direction, and come and take refuge in the Lord, for it is an everlasting covenant, and they will not forget.
My people became like lost sheep. Their shepherds drove them away and led them astray on the mountains. They went from mountain to hill and forgot their resting places.

Everyone who found them destroyed them. Their enemies said, “Let us not spare them, because they sinned against the Lord, who is the pasture of righteousness, and against the Lord who gathered their fathers.”
Depart from the midst of Babylon and come out of the land of the Chaldeans. Be like male goats at the head of the flocks.

For look, I will raise up and bring against the Babylonians an assembly of great nations from the northern land. They will array themselves against her, and from there she will be captured, like the arrow of a skilled warrior that does not return empty.
The land of the Chaldeans will become plunder, and all who plunder it will have their fill, says the Lord.
For you rejoiced and boasted as you plundered my inheritance. You leaped like calves on the green grass and fought like bulls.
Your mother was greatly put to shame, the mother who had been prosperous. Look, she is the last of the nations—a desolate, waterless wilderness.
Because of the Lord’s anger, it will not be inhabited, but will become entirely desolate. Everyone who passes through Babylon will be distressed and hiss at all its wounds.
Array yourselves all around Babylon, all you archers. Shoot at her and do not spare your arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord.

Raise a shout all around her, for her hands have gone limp, her towers have fallen, and her walls have been demolished. For this is vengeance from God. Take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.
Destroy the offspring in Babylon and the one who takes up the sickle at harvest time. Before the Greek sword, let each return to his own people and each flee to his own land.
Israel is a straying sheep; lions drove him away. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and afterward the king of Babylon devoured his bones.
Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I will take vengeance on the king of Babylon and his land, just as I took vengeance on the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to safety in his pastures. He will graze on Carmel and in Bashan, and on the mountain of Ephraim and in Gilead they will have their fill.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord, they will search for Israel’s wrongdoing, but it will no longer exist, and for Judah’s sins, but they will not be found, for I will atone for their wrongdoing upon the earth.
Go up against her with bitterness and take vengeance on her inhabitants. Let sword and destruction follow her, says the Lord, and do everything that I commanded you.
The sound of war comes from the land of the Chaldeans, and great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth has been broken and shattered! How Babylon has become a ruin among the nations!
They will attack you, and you will be captured, Babylon, without knowing it. You were found and captured because you turned against the Lord.
The Lord opened his treasuries and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Lord of hosts has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Her times have come upon her. Open her storehouses; search her as you would caves, and destroy her. Let no survivors remain among them.
Dry up all her produce, and let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of vengeance upon them!
The sound of those who have fled and escaped from the land of the Babylonians, proclaiming in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, the vengeance for his temple.

Give orders to the multitudes, to all the archers, against Babylon: “Camp all around her, so that no one may escape from her. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her everything she has done, for she has opposed the Lord, the God, the Holy One of Israel.”
Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her warriors will fall and lie there on that day, says the Lord.
Look, I am against you, you proud one, says the Lord of hosts, for your day has come, the time of your punishment.
Your pride will grow weak and fall, and no one will raise it up. I will kindle a fire in her forests, and it will consume everything around her.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: The children of Israel and the children of Judah have been oppressed. All who took them captive held them by force and would not release them.
The one who redeemed them is mighty; the Lord Almighty is his name. He will plead his case against his adversaries, so that he may lift up the earth and be angry with the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword against the Chaldeans, says the Lord, and against the inhabitants of Babylon, against all her great men, and against her counselors.
A sword against her desires, and they will be taken away; a sword against her warriors, and they will lose heart.

A sword against her horses and her chariots; a sword against their champions and against all the mixed multitude within her, and they will become like women. A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered.
A sword against her waters, and they will be put to shame, for it is a land of carved images, and against the islands in which they boasted.
Therefore monsters will dwell on the islands, and daughters of sirens will dwell in her. She will never again be rebuilt or inhabited.
Just as God destroyed the land of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring territories, says the Lord, no one will live there, and no human being will stay there.
Look, a force is coming from the north, a great nation, and many kings will rise from the ends of the earth.

With a bow in his hand and armed with a spear, he is ruthless and will show no mercy. Their voice will roar like the sea. They are mounted on horses, prepared like fire for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon heard the news of them, and his hands grew weak. Distress seized him, pain like that of a woman in labor.

Look, like a lion he will come up from the rushing waters of the Jordan to the place of Etham, for very swiftly I will drive them away from it, and I will raise up all the young men against her. For who is like me? Who will oppose me? What shepherd will stand against me?

Therefore hear the Lord’s plan that he has devised against Babylon, and his purposes that he has devised against the inhabitants of Chaldea. Will you not destroy the lambs of their flocks? Will their pastures not be destroyed by them?
For at the sound of Babylon’s collapse the earth will shake, and the news of her disaster will be heard among the nations.
Thus says the Lord: Look, I will raise up against Babylon and against her inhabitants the heart of those who rise up, and a destructive, scorching wind.
I will send revilers to Babylon, and they will revile her and destroy her land, for woe is upon Babylon on every side on the day of her suffering.
Let the one who is to draw the bow draw his bow, and let whoever has weapons arm himself. Do not spare her young men, and destroy her entire army.
The wounded will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and those pierced through will fall all around her.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, the Lord Almighty, though their land has been filled with lawlessness against the holy things of Israel.

Flee from the midst of Babylon, and let each of you save your own life. Do not be destroyed because of her wrongdoing, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance upon her; he himself will repay her.
Babylon is a golden cup in the Lord's hand, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations were shaken.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament over her; fetch medicine for her wounds. Perhaps she may be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her, and let each of us go to our own land, for the judgments against her have reached heaven and risen to the stars.
And the Lord brought judgment upon her. Come, let us recount in Zion the works of the Lord our God.

Prepare the bows; fill the quivers, for the Lord has stirred up the spirit of the king of the Medes. His anger is against Babylon, and he will destroy her, for this is the Lord's vengeance, vengeance for his temple.
Raise a banner against Babylon's walls. Set guards, awaken the sentries, and prepare the weapons, for the Lord has set to work and will accomplish what he spoke against Babylon's inhabitants.
You who dwell beside abundant waters, amid the abundance of her treasures, your end has come; truly and surely it has entered your belly.
For the Lord of hosts swore by his own arm: 'I will fill you with troops like locusts, and those who descend upon you will raise a shout over you.'
He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
At his voice he set a multitude of roaring waters in the heavens. He brings up clouds from the ends of the earth, made lightning for the rain, and brought light out of his storehouses.
Every person has become foolish through knowledge. Every goldsmith has been put to shame by his carved images, for they cast falsehood, and there is no spirit in them.
They are worthless, works of mockery; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like this, for the one who created everything is his portion and the staff of his inheritance. The Lord of hosts is his name.
You shall scatter your weapons of war for me, and through you I will scatter nations and remove kings from your midst.
And I will scatter his cavalry in you, and I will scatter his chariots and their riders upon you.
Through you I will scatter man and woman; through you I will scatter the old and the young; through you I will scatter the chosen man and the virgin.
Through you I will scatter the shepherd and his flock; through you I will scatter the farmer and his farming; through you I will scatter your commanders and military leaders.
'I will repay Babylon and the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did to Zion before your eyes,' says the Lord.

'Look, I am against you, destroying mountain,' says the Lord, 'you who destroyed the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burned mountain.'
'They will no longer take from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, for you will be a ruin forever,' says the Lord.

Raise a banner over the land; blow the trumpet among all the nations. Summon troops against her. Give a command from me to the kingdoms of Ararat and the force of Ashkenaz. Station archers against her; advance against [?]. It was shaken and tormented, for the Lord's plan came upon Babylon—horses like a multitude of locusts.
Summon against her the nations and the king of the Medes, his commanders and all their military leaders, to that place, and all the rulers of the earth.
To make the land of Babylon desolate, so that no one will dwell in it.
The warriors of Babylon have ceased fighting; they will sit under siege. Their strength has broken, and they have become like women. Her houses have been set on fire; their bars have been shattered.
Fugitive will meet fugitive, and messenger will encounter messenger, to bring bad news to the king of Babylon that his city has been taken and its exits have been seized at its edges.
Their assemblies were burned with fire, and the fighting men rushed to the gates.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: The house of Babylon will stand like a threshing floor [?]; in a little while its harvest will come.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me, came against me, and tore me apart. He made me like an empty vessel; he swallowed me like a dragon and filled his belly with my delicacies.
“My labors were cast away, and my sufferings went to Babylon,” the inhabitant of Zion will say. “My blood is upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,” Jerusalem will say.
Therefore the Lord says this: “Look, I will judge your adversary and seek vengeance for you. I will lay waste her sea and dry up her springs.”
Babylon will become heaps of ruins, a dwelling place for dragons, a place of destruction and hissing, and no one will live there.
Together their sons made themselves ready like lions and like lion cubs.
“In the heat of their spears I will give them terrors, and I will make them drunk, so that they become numb and sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake,” says the Lord.
Bring them down like sheep to slaughter, and like rams together with goats.
How you have been defeated, Sheshach, and caught in a trap, you who were the boast of all the earth! How Babylon has become a desolation among all the nations!
The sea rose over Babylon; she was covered by its roaring waves.
Her cities became a place of destruction, a waterless land and a wilderness. No one will live in it, and no human being will rest there.
“I will seek vengeance on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he swallowed. Nations will no longer gather to him.” Even the walls of Babylon have fallen.
Come out of her midst, my people, and let each of you save your life from the Lord’s fierce anger.

Never let your hearts falter, and do not fear the reports you hear in the land, for a report will come in that year, and after that year another report, and injustice in the land, proverb upon proverb.
“Therefore, look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will bring judgment upon the carved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her wounded will fall within her.”
Heaven and earth and everything in them will rejoice over Babylon, for those who bring her misery will come from the north, says the Lord.
In Babylon the wounded of all the earth will fall.
You survivors, come out of that land; do not remain. You who are far away, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem come into your hearts.
We were put to shame because we heard our reproach. Dishonor covered our faces, for foreigners entered our holy places in the house of the Lord.
“Therefore, look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will seek vengeance on her carved images, and the wounded will fall throughout the land.”
“Even if Babylon rises as high as heaven, and even if she fortifies the height of her strength, destroyers will come upon her from me,” says the Lord.
A sound of bad news comes from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans.
For the Lord destroyed Babylon and removed the great voice from her. The roar of their waves, like many waters, sounded her destruction.
For disaster came upon Babylon. Her armed men were captured, and her archers were terrified, for God is a God of repayment; the Lord himself repays her what she is due.

And he will make her commanders and her wise men, her rulers and her army chiefs and her warriors drunk, and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake, says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.

The Lord of hosts says this: “The wall of Babylon was widened; it will be utterly demolished, and her high gates will be burned with fire. Peoples will labor in vain, and a nation will be destroyed at the beginning.”

The word that the Lord commanded the prophet Jeremiah to speak to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, when he went from King Zedekiah of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was his official in charge of gifts.
And Jeremiah wrote in one book all the calamities that were to come upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you go to Babylon and see it, read all these words aloud
and say, ‘Lord, you have spoken against this place, to destroy it so that no inhabitant remains in it, either human or animal, for it will be a ruin forever.’
When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates
and say, ‘Thus Babylon will sink and never rise from the disasters that I will bring upon it.’” Here the words of the prophet Jeremiah ended.
King Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did evil before the Lord, as Jehoiakim had done.
For Jerusalem and Judah were under the Lord’s anger until he cast them out of his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

And in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem with his entire army and besieged it. He built walls around it, wall beside wall, out of squared stones.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and no bread could be found for the people of the land to eat.

The city was breached, and all the fighting men fled and left the city by night by the road through the gate, along the wall and through the window on the side of the royal garden. The Chaldeans were surrounding the city, and the men went by the road of the Arabs.
The army of the king of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook King Zedekiah at the crossings of Jericho. All his servants scattered away from him.
And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed judgment on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
He blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him with shackles. The king of Babylon took him to Babylon and put him in the millhouse until the day of his death.
In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, who served before the king of Babylon, came
and set fire to the house of the Lord, the royal palaces, and all the houses of the city. He burned all the great palaces with fire.
All the Chaldean troops who were with the captain of the guard demolished the entire wall surrounding Jerusalem.

But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poor people and some of the survivors, the destitute who remained in the city, the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the people.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poor of the land as vineyard workers and cultivators.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the Lord, the bases, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and carried all the bronze to Babylon.
He took the feet, the upper bases, the capitals, the basins, the meat hooks, and all the bronze utensils used for service,
and the [?], the [?], the basins, the lampstands, the cups, and the boxes. The captain of the guard took those made of gold as gold and those made of silver as silver.
And there were two pillars, one Sea, and twelve bulls that stood beneath the Sea, which King Solomon had made in the house of the Lord. The bronze and all the bronze furnishings were beyond measure.
Each pillar was thirty-five cubits high, and a band of twelve cubits encircled it. Its thickness all around was four fingers.

Its capitals were bronze, and the height of one capital was five cubits. The latticework and pomegranate ornaments around the capital were all bronze. The second pillar was of the same design: eight pomegranate ornaments, cubit by cubit, in twelve cubits [?].
There were ninety-six pomegranate ornaments on one side, and there were a hundred pomegranate ornaments in all around the latticework.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three gatekeepers.

From the city he took one eunuch who was in charge of the fighting men, seven distinguished men who attended the king and were found in the city, the chief scribe, the commander of the troops, and the chief scribe of the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was taken captive from its own land.
These are the people whom King Nebuchadnezzar took captive: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews;
and in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, they took away eight hundred and thirty-two people from Jerusalem;
and in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard deported seven hundred and forty-five Jews. There were four thousand and six hundred people in all.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, raised up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of the house where he was held in custody.
He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
He changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually in his presence for all the days that he lived.
A regular daily allowance was assigned to him, which was given by the king of Babylon day by day until the day of his death, for all the days of his life.
